ideas.rationale: The package signals done-ness by colour, so the user needs no instructions or sensors.

ideas.title: Barcode Cook Programs

new_nodes.label: Barcode scanner window
new_nodes.detail: Scans the food packet barcode and loads the correct cooking program.

ideas.rationale: The packet tells the oven what to do, so students never have to read or set anything.

ideas.title: Presence-Based Standby

new_nodes.label: Radar presence sensor
new_nodes.detail: Radar detects a person nearby and wakes the display, otherwise the oven stays dark.

ideas.rationale: The oven responds to a person walking up, so no power button needs finding.

ideas.title: Single Big Button Oven

new_nodes.label: One-button control
new_nodes.detail: One large button starts a default auto-cook that reheats most foods.

ideas.rationale: A single button with a sensible default means there is nothing to learn at all.

ideas.title: Voice-Less Sizzle Alert

new_nodes.label: Sizzle sound cue
new_nodes.detail: A short realistic sizzle sound plays when food is done instead of a bell.

ideas.rationale: A sound people recognise from cooking needs no explanation, unlike a bell with no context.

ideas.title: Vibrating Handle Timer

new_nodes.label: Handle buzz motor
new_nodes.detail: A small vibration motor in the handle buzzes to signal that cooking is finished.

ideas.rationale: A buzz in the hand is felt even by someone who has the kitchen radio on.

ideas.title: Ambient Light Done Ring

new_nodes.label: Ring light progress
new_nodes.detail: A ring of LEDs around the top fills as cooking progresses and turns green when done.

ideas.rationale: A visual progress ring explains the state of the oven at a glance.

ideas.title: Mood Light Cavity

new_nodes.label: Cooking mood glow
new_nodes.detail: Cavity glows warm amber while heating and cool white when finished.

ideas.rationale: Colour communicates state without words, so the user always knows what the oven is doing.

ideas.title: Projected Door Display

new_nodes.label: Door projector
new_nodes.detail: Projects simple icons onto the door glass showing mode and time remaining.

ideas.rationale: Information shown on the door where the food is removes the need to look at a separate panel.

ideas.title: Ceramic Susceptor Plate

new_nodes.label: Silicon carbide heat plate
new_nodes.detail: A ceramic plate absorbs microwaves and gets hot enough to brown food from below.

ideas.rationale: Browning food from below with a plate removes the need for users to know any special browning settings.

ideas.title: Fixed Plate No Turntable

new_nodes.label: Multi-antenna field shaping
new_nodes.detail: Several small antennas shape the field so food heats evenly on a fixed plate.

ideas.rationale: Without a turntable, there is nothing to jam, clean, or misplace, so the oven is simpler to use.

ideas.title: Robotic Food Tray

new_nodes.label: Self-positioning tray
new_nodes.detail: Tray moves food to the best heating spot automatically.

ideas.rationale: The machine positions the food itself, so the user never has to think about placement.

ideas.title: Stir Pulse Anti-Boil

new_nodes.label: Auto stir pulse
new_nodes.detail: Short bursts of heat with a pause and a vibrating tray break up superheating.

ideas.rationale: Superheating is prevented automatically, so the user never needs to know about eruptive boiling.

ideas.title: Self-Limiting Liquid Mode

new_nodes.label: Surface boiling detector
new_nodes.detail: Detects first bubbles and cuts power before the liquid can superheat.

ideas.rationale: The oven stops at the right point for liquids, so no one has to guess how long a drink needs.

ideas.title: Battery Cordless Puck

new_nodes.label: Magnetic charging puck
new_nodes.detail: The oven base snaps onto a wall or counter puck that charges it without any cord.

ideas.rationale: Snapping the oven onto a puck removes cord plugging and the mains question altogether.

ideas.title: Wireless Power Oven

new_nodes.label: Resonant wireless power
new_nodes.detail: The oven draws power from a flat mat on the counter without any plug.

ideas.rationale: Placing the oven on a mat is the simplest connection possible, so no one has to find a socket.

ideas.title: Stamped Metal Replaced By Molded Shell

new_nodes.label: Molded recycled shell
new_nodes.detail: Shell is moulded from recycled fibre and polymer instead of stamped steel.

ideas.rationale: A lighter, cheaper shell keeps the oven affordable and easy to lift for any student.

ideas.title: Foam Chassis Oven

new_nodes.label: Foam-moulded chassis
new_nodes.detail: Interior chassis is a single moulded foam part with snap fit wiring channels.

ideas.rationale: Fewer parts make assembly cheaper and mean fewer things to go wrong for the user.

ideas.title: Magnetic Door Seal Instead Of Choke

new_nodes.label: Magnetic seal strip
new_nodes.detail: Flexible magnetic strip keeps the door sealed and reads closure for the interlock.

ideas.rationale: One part both seals and senses the door, so there are fewer parts to misunderstand.

ideas.title: Single Hall Sensor Interlock

new_nodes.label: Hall effect door sensor
new_nodes.detail: One solid-state sensor replaces three microswitches and reports door state.

ideas.rationale: A simpler sensor cuts the chance of a confusing fault, so the oven just works when closed.

ideas.title: Ceramic Mica Replaced By Film

new_nodes.label: Self-cleaning ceramic film
new_nodes.detail: A thin ceramic film on the cavity wall repels splatter and cleans itself.

ideas.rationale: A wall that cleans itself removes the cleaning routine, which is one thing users get wrong.

ideas.title: Wipe-Free Cavity

new_nodes.label: Auto steam clean
new_nodes.detail: Oven runs a steam cycle after each use that loosens food residue.

ideas.rationale: Cleaning happens by itself, so the user never needs a cleaning instruction.

ideas.title: Thermostat Replaced By IR Spot Sensor

new_nodes.label: Infrared spot sensor
new_nodes.detail: Non-contact sensor reads food and cavity temperature to protect the magnetron.

ideas.rationale: A sensor with no moving parts protects the oven without any user action.

ideas.title: Self-Resetting Overheat Guard

new_nodes.label: Polymer PTC safety fuse
new_nodes.detail: Polymer switch trips when too hot and resets when cool with no user action.

ideas.rationale: A fuse that resets itself means no one ever has to reset or repair anything.

ideas.title: Cook-Anything Universal Mode

new_nodes.label: Universal auto heat
new_nodes.detail: One mode senses food type and heats anything without choosing a setting.

ideas.rationale: Users never choose a mode because the oven decides for every food.

ideas.title: Two-Button Cook Or Stop

new_nodes.label: Cook and stop keys
new_nodes.detail: Only a large green and red key remain, with no other controls.

ideas.rationale: Two self-explanatory keys cover the entire experience with no possibility of confusion.

ideas.title: Food Recipe Cartridge

new_nodes.label: Recipe cartridge slot
new_nodes.detail: Insert a cartridge with the food's settings printed as a code and the oven does the rest.

ideas.rationale: Inserting a cartridge is more obvious than programming, so students never need a manual.

ideas.title: Hot Plate Tray With Heat Memory

new_nodes.label: Phase-change heat tray
new_nodes.detail: Tray stores heat and releases it evenly so food keeps warm after cooking.

ideas.rationale: The tray keeps food warm automatically, so users never have to reheat or set a hold mode.

ideas.title: Hold-Warm By Default

new_nodes.label: Auto keep warm
new_nodes.detail: Food stays at serving temperature until the door is opened.

ideas.rationale: Keeping food warm by default removes the need to decide when to take it out.

ideas.title: Grease-Proof Cavity Coating

new_nodes.label: Non-stick ceramic coating
new_nodes.detail: Smooth glass-ceramic coating stops food sticking and makes wiping trivial.

ideas.rationale: Food that does not stick means no scrubbing, which is the most common frustration for students.

ideas.title: Container-Agnostic Arc Shield

new_nodes.label: Arc-tolerant cavity
new_nodes.detail: Cavity design tolerates small metal items without arcing so users need not check containers.

ideas.rationale: Users can put in any dish without a rule to memorise, which removes an entire category of mistakes.

ideas.title: Fridge-Door Mounted Oven

new_nodes.label: Magnetic fridge-door microwave
new_nodes.detail: Compact unit clips to the fridge door and heats food from the fridge.

ideas.rationale: Food is reheated where it is already stored, so no counter setup or moving of plates is needed.

ideas.title: Shared Hub Microwave

new_nodes.label: Dorm hub microwave
new_nodes.detail: Shared appliance with a single one-tap screen and a drop-in tray that anyone can use.

ideas.rationale: A single shared unit with one tap suits students who share kitchens and have no time to learn settings.

ideas.title: Dish Shaped Cavity Walls

new_nodes.label: Self-aligning cradle
new_nodes.detail: A cradle shaped to the common plate size centres any dish automatically.

ideas.rationale: A dish that centres itself needs no thought about placement or uneven heating.

ideas.title: Pocket-Size Lunch Oven

new_nodes.label: Lunchbox microwave
new_nodes.detail: Small heated box with a single lid button sized for one meal.

ideas.rationale: A box that is the container removes the need for transferring food and any setting choices.

ideas.title: Read-Your-Mind Cooking Assistant

new_nodes.label: Single question interface
new_nodes.detail: Oven asks just Hot or Cold and handles everything else.

ideas.rationale: Reducing every choice to one plain question means there is no learning curve at all.

ideas.title: Pet-Free Smell Alarm

new_nodes.label: Smoke and burn detector
new_nodes.detail: Detects smoke or burning and stops heating while showing a simple red light.

ideas.rationale: The oven catches mistakes itself, so users do not need to know what overcooking looks like.

ideas.title: Glove-Friendly Touch Tabs

new_nodes.label: Oversized door tab
new_nodes.detail: Large tab sticks out from the door edge and is easy to grab with an oven mitt.

ideas.rationale: A large obvious tab works with any hand, glove, or distraction, so opening always feels obvious.

ideas.title: Steam-sensing auto-stop

new_nodes.label: Steam-sensing auto-stop probe
new_nodes.detail: Humidity sensor in cavity ceiling detects steam rise and ends cooking when food is done.

ideas.rationale: The user never sets a time, so there is nothing to learn or misjudge.

ideas.title: Food-photo button menu

new_nodes.label: Four large food-photo buttons
new_nodes.detail: Raised buttons showing photos of popcorn, rice, soup and leftovers, each starting a preset.

ideas.rationale: Users recognise a picture of their food faster than they read a number on a dial.

ideas.title: Camera food recognition

new_nodes.label: Cavity camera with food classifier
new_nodes.detail: Small camera identifies the food on the turntable and sets time and power automatically.

ideas.rationale: Both knobs disappear, so the only task left is putting food in and pressing start.

ideas.title: Tap-to-add-30-seconds button

new_nodes.label: Single tap-counter button
new_nodes.detail: Each press adds 30 seconds, and a long press starts cooking.

ideas.rationale: Counting taps needs no reading or arithmetic, and it removes the timer's imprecision for short durations.

ideas.title: Load-cell weight-loss stop

new_nodes.label: Turntable load cell
new_nodes.detail: Strain gauge under the turntable measures mass loss from evaporation and stops when the target is reached.

ideas.rationale: The machine stops by itself based on what happens to the food, so the user never has to estimate minutes.

ideas.title: Sand-hourglass timer

new_nodes.label: Visible sand-glass timer
new_nodes.detail: A clear tube with fine sand sits on the door top and drains as cooking proceeds.

ideas.rationale: Remaining time is shown as a falling pile of sand that anyone can read at a glance.

ideas.title: Door-close starts, door-open stops

new_nodes.label: Door-closure sensor
new_nodes.detail: Magnetic reed switch starts cooking when the door shuts and stops it when the door opens.

ideas.rationale: Closing the door is the only action needed, which matches the habit of shutting something to make it work.

ideas.title: NFC food-packet programming

new_nodes.label: NFC food-packet tags
new_nodes.detail: Ready meals carry tags that send cooking time and power settings when touched to the panel.

ideas.rationale: Users tap the packet to the machine and never choose a setting themselves.

ideas.title: Thermochromic door progress ring

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic door ring
new_nodes.detail: Heat-sensitive ink on the door window changes colour from blue to red as food heats.

ideas.rationale: Colour progress is understood without any reading, so the user can judge doneness without knowing any settings.

ideas.title: Vibrating handle instead of bell

new_nodes.label: Haptic handle pulse
new_nodes.detail: A small vibration motor in the door handle buzzes when cooking ends.

ideas.rationale: A pulse in the hand is noticed even by users with hearing loss and needs no understanding of a bell.

ideas.title: Turntable ring-light progress

new_nodes.label: LED ring under turntable
new_nodes.detail: A ring of LEDs around the glass base depletes as cooking progresses.

ideas.rationale: A shrinking ring of light shows how much time remains without any numbers to interpret.

ideas.title: Single heat slider with food icons

new_nodes.label: Food-icon heat slider
new_nodes.detail: One slider moves between a soft icon, a bowl icon and a steak icon, setting power to match.

ideas.rationale: Choosing by what the food is replaces understanding of power percentages.

ideas.title: Inverter hides duty cycle

new_nodes.label: Inverter-driven magnetron
new_nodes.detail: Variable-frequency drive gives continuous power so the user never sees on-off cycling.

ideas.rationale: Continuous heating removes the cycling that confused users and makes the power setting feel simple.

ideas.title: Traffic-light power dial

new_nodes.label: Three-colour power dial
new_nodes.detail: A dial with green for gentle, amber for normal and red for hot.

ideas.rationale: Colour meanings are universal and need no training, so the power level is clear immediately.

ideas.title: Automatic keep-warm hold

new_nodes.label: Hold serving temperature
new_nodes.detail: After cooking, the cavity holds food at a warm temperature until it is removed.

ideas.rationale: Users need no decision about when to stop, because the food stays warm until they return.

ideas.title: Placemat heat glow

new_nodes.label: Glowing placemat indicator
new_nodes.detail: Brightness of a glow strip on the top panel shows heat intensity as it changes.

ideas.rationale: Brighter means hotter, which is a mapping any user already understands.

ideas.title: Smell-sensing reheat

new_nodes.label: Volatile-gas sensor
new_nodes.detail: Gas sensor detects aroma rising from food and lowers power when it peaks.

ideas.rationale: Sensing the food itself means the user never sets power at all.

ideas.title: Transparent conductive window

new_nodes.label: Transparent conductive film
new_nodes.detail: Indium-tin-oxide coating on glass blocks microwaves while staying clear to view.

ideas.rationale: A clear window shows the food without a mesh that gets dirty and confuses users.

ideas.title: Cavity camera on the front screen

new_nodes.label: Cavity camera and screen
new_nodes.detail: A camera inside shows a live picture of the food on a small screen on the front.

ideas.rationale: Users check food by looking at a screen they already trust, not by bending to peer through a door.

ideas.title: Sliding drawer door

new_nodes.label: Sliding drawer front
new_nodes.detail: The whole front slides out like a drawer, with no hinge or swing arc.

ideas.rationale: A drawer is opened by pulling, which is the most obvious action there is.

ideas.title: Toaster-style lift lid

new_nodes.label: Vertical lift lid
new_nodes.detail: The top lifts straight up on a counterweight, like a toaster lid.

ideas.rationale: Lifting a lid is an everyday motion, so no one has to learn how a door works.

ideas.title: Proximity auto-open door

new_nodes.label: Proximity sensor door opener
new_nodes.detail: An infrared sensor opens the door when a hand is brought close to the handle.

ideas.rationale: The door opens without any button to find or press, which suits users with weak grip or poor sight.

ideas.title: Flush magnetic touch door

new_nodes.label: Magnetic flush latch
new_nodes.detail: A flat front pushed lightly opens on a magnet and closes with a soft click.

ideas.rationale: Pushing anywhere on a flat front opens the door, so there is no button location to remember.

ideas.title: Laptop-style clamshell lid

new_nodes.label: Clamshell top lid
new_nodes.detail: The top lifts on a hinge like a laptop screen, with a built-in handle.

ideas.rationale: People already know how to open a laptop lid, so the gesture is instantly familiar.

ideas.title: Pull-handle with no button

new_nodes.label: Spring-loaded pull handle
new_nodes.detail: A handle pulled outward releases the latch mechanically, with no button.

ideas.rationale: A pull action needs no label or instruction and uses the same motion as any cupboard.

ideas.title: Glowing green touch pad

new_nodes.label: Green-lit touch pad
new_nodes.detail: A large capacitive pad glows green when ready and opens the door when touched.

ideas.rationale: A green glow tells the user the machine is ready, so there is nothing to guess.

ideas.title: Hand-wave door opener

new_nodes.label: Wave-sensing door opener
new_nodes.detail: A radar sensor opens the door when a hand is waved in front of the panel.

ideas.rationale: A wave is a gesture almost anyone can perform without training.

ideas.title: One-piece silicone living hinge

new_nodes.label: Moulded silicone hinge
new_nodes.detail: The door and frame are one moulded part joined by a flexible silicone strip.

ideas.rationale: A single moulded part is cheaper to build and cannot wear loose, so the door always opens predictably.

ideas.title: Magnetic floating door

new_nodes.label: Magnetic floating hinge
new_nodes.detail: Magnets hold the door in place and guide it open and shut without mechanical hinges.

ideas.rationale: The door floats shut with a gentle pull, which is easy for anyone to use.

ideas.title: Moulded conductive polymer cavity

new_nodes.label: Conductive-coated polymer moulding
new_nodes.detail: Injection-moulded polymer with a conductive metallic coating replaces stamped steel.

ideas.rationale: A cheaper shape lets the product stay low cost, which keeps simple machines available to elderly buyers.

ideas.title: Self-stirring antenna replaces turntable

new_nodes.label: Rotating mode stirrer
new_nodes.detail: A moving metal vane spreads microwaves so food heats evenly with no turntable to fit.

ideas.rationale: Users no longer need to place the glass plate correctly or wash it, so there is one less step.

ideas.title: Reusable silicone tray with guide pattern

new_nodes.label: Guide-pattern silicone tray
new_nodes.detail: A flexible tray with a printed centre mark shows where to place food.

ideas.rationale: A printed guide shows the user exactly where food goes without any instruction.

ideas.title: Self-glowing cavity walls

new_nodes.label: Phosphorescent cavity lining
new_nodes.detail: Glow-in-the-dark coating on the cavity walls lights the food for a while after the door opens.

ideas.rationale: Light without a bulb needs no switch or replacement, which removes a maintenance task.

ideas.title: Thermal camera view

new_nodes.label: Thermal-image window
new_nodes.detail: A thermal camera shows the food's hot spots in colour on the front panel.

ideas.rationale: Hot and cold areas are shown as colour, so the user sees what is done without opening the door.

ideas.title: One-button auto-program

new_nodes.label: Single start button
new_nodes.detail: One large button starts cooking, using sensors to choose time and power.

ideas.rationale: A single button means the whole control panel is one action and nothing else to learn.

ideas.title: Countertop drawer unit

new_nodes.label: Built-in drawer microwave
new_nodes.detail: The microwave slides into a cabinet drawer at counter height, with no lifting.

ideas.rationale: Keeping the oven at waist height removes reaching and lifting, which are hard for older users.

ideas.title: NFC tap plate with one button

new_nodes.label: NFC tap pad
new_nodes.detail: A pad on the top reads a tagged plate or packet and starts the right programme.

ideas.rationale: Tapping a plate is the only interaction needed, which means there is nothing to learn.

ideas.title: Plate-on-tray food reader

new_nodes.label: Weight-and-shape tray
new_nodes.detail: The tray reads the weight and shape of the placed plate and sets the programme.

ideas.rationale: Placing the plate is the input, so the user never picks a setting.

ideas.title: Voice commands

new_nodes.label: Simple voice command set
new_nodes.detail: Speaking short words like warm, reheat or done selects the programme.

ideas.rationale: Speaking a plain word needs no panel reading, which suits users with poor eyesight.

ideas.title: Pictogram-only labels

new_nodes.label: Universal pictogram panel
new_nodes.detail: The panel uses only pictograms and colour, with no printed words or numbers.

ideas.rationale: Pictograms are readable across languages and ages without any written instruction.

ideas.title: Rotating icon drum replaces both knobs

new_nodes.label: Food-icon drum
new_nodes.detail: A single rotating drum shows food icons, and turning it sets both time and power.

ideas.rationale: One control with pictures replaces two dials with numbers, which is simpler to use.

ideas.title: Light-pulse done cue

new_nodes.label: Pulsing done light
new_nodes.detail: A green light pulses on the top panel until the door is opened.

ideas.rationale: A pulsing light keeps signalling until the user acts, so nobody misses that food is ready.

ideas.title: Universal voltage power supply

new_nodes.label: Wide-input GaN power supply
new_nodes.detail: Gallium nitride supply accepts any mains voltage and frequency without a setting.

ideas.rationale: No voltage or frequency selection is needed, so setup is plug in and use.

ideas.title: Reheat-only appliance

new_nodes.label: Single reheat function
new_nodes.detail: The machine has one reheat mode and no separate cooking modes.

ideas.rationale: Removing every mode except reheat means there is nothing to choose.

ideas.title: Large sealed membrane panel

new_nodes.label: Raised membrane button
new_nodes.detail: A sealed, wipeable panel with one large raised button that clicks when pressed.

ideas.rationale: A large tactile button is easy to find and press, and the sealed surface resists spills.

ideas.title: Preset per food programme

new_nodes.label: Food preset buttons
new_nodes.detail: Each common food has its own button that sets time and power in one press.

ideas.rationale: Each food has its own button, so nothing needs to be calculated.

ideas.title: Gesture-controlled door start

new_nodes.label: Swipe-to-start gesture pad
new_nodes.detail: A swipe across the front panel starts cooking without pressing any button.

ideas.rationale: A swipe is a gesture learned from phones and needs no button to find.

ideas.title: Induction-style heating plate

new_nodes.label: Heated plate base
new_nodes.detail: Food sits on a plate that the machine heats directly, with no cavity to manage.

ideas.rationale: Placing a plate on a heated base needs no door, timer or power setting.

ideas.title: Self-closing door

new_nodes.label: Spring self-closer
new_nodes.detail: A spring returns the door fully shut after release, so it cannot be left open.

ideas.rationale: The door always closes on its own, so the user never needs to check it is sealed.

ideas.title: Door-sensing cut-off replaces interlock

new_nodes.label: Solid-state door sensor
new_nodes.detail: A solid-state sensor cuts power the moment the door opens, with no mechanical interlock.

ideas.rationale: A safety cut-off that works without any user action keeps operation simple and safe for elderly users.

ideas.title: Single Picture Dial

new_nodes.label: Picture dial with 4 food icons
new_nodes.detail: One rotating dial showing pictures (soup, frozen meal, drink, reheat) that sets time and power together.

ideas.rationale: Users choose a picture of what they are cooking instead of deciding on minutes and power levels.

ideas.title: Hourglass Sand Timer

new_nodes.label: Visible sand-fill timer column
new_nodes.detail: A clear column whose sand level drops as cooking proceeds, so time is seen, not read.

ideas.rationale: Remaining time is shown by a physical level that needs no numbers or reading skill.

ideas.title: Food Card Slot

new_nodes.label: Printed food-card slot
new_nodes.detail: Slide a credit-card-sized printed card showing the food; its magnetic stripe sets time and power.

ideas.rationale: Inserting a card that matches the food removes all settings the user must learn.

ideas.title: Food-Weight Auto Power

new_nodes.label: Load-cell turntable sensor
new_nodes.detail: Strain gauges under the turntable weigh the food and choose power and time automatically.

ideas.rationale: Placing food on the plate is the only action, because the machine works out the settings from its weight.

ideas.title: One-Dome Start Button

new_nodes.label: Single domed start button
new_nodes.detail: One large dome press starts cooking at a default setting; pressing again adds 30 seconds.

ideas.rationale: A single obvious button means nothing needs to be learned before the first use.

ideas.title: Humidity-Ended Cooking

new_nodes.label: Steam humidity sensor
new_nodes.detail: A humidity sensor in the vent stops the cycle when steam output peaks and falls.

ideas.rationale: The user never sets a time because the food itself signals when it is done.

ideas.title: Electroluminescent Cavity Glow

new_nodes.label: Electroluminescent wall film
new_nodes.detail: A thin, cool, low-voltage glowing film on the cavity wall replaces the 25 W bulb.

ideas.rationale: The light is always on the surface, so the user never has to find or replace a bulb.

ideas.title: Glowing Cooking-Status Wall

new_nodes.label: Colour-shifting status wall
new_nodes.detail: Cavity walls shift colour from cool blue to warm amber as the food heats.

ideas.rationale: Colour gives status at a glance, so no reading of numbers or dials is needed.

ideas.title: Haptic Handle Ding

new_nodes.label: Handle vibration pulse motor
new_nodes.detail: A small vibration motor in the door handle buzzes three times at the end of cooking.

ideas.rationale: A felt pulse signals completion to users who cannot see the screen or hear a bell.

ideas.title: Scented Done Signal

new_nodes.label: Cooking-done scent cartridge
new_nodes.detail: A small cartridge releases a mild, pleasant scent when cooking finishes.

ideas.rationale: A distinct smell reaches the user in any room and needs no learned meaning.

ideas.title: Spoken Ready Voice

new_nodes.label: Single-phrase speaker
new_nodes.detail: A tiny speaker says 'Ready, take it out' in a calm voice when cooking ends.

ideas.rationale: A plain spoken message needs no interpretation, which suits older and visually impaired users.

ideas.title: Door Shell Touch-to-Open

new_nodes.label: Full-door touch panel
new_nodes.detail: The whole door face opens on a light push, with no button or latch to find.

ideas.rationale: Pushing anywhere on the door opens it, so the user never has to search for a button.

ideas.title: Spring-Push Door

new_nodes.label: Spring-loaded push door
new_nodes.detail: A spring-loaded hinge opens the door a few centimetres when pressed, no latch needed.

ideas.rationale: A gentle push is the natural way to open a door, so no mechanism needs learning.

ideas.title: Hip-Bump Door Release

new_nodes.label: Kick-plate door sensor
new_nodes.detail: A low kick plate senses a foot or hip and releases the door.

ideas.rationale: Users with full hands can open the door with a bump, reducing the need for precise button use.

ideas.title: Drawer Microwave

new_nodes.label: Sliding drawer front
new_nodes.detail: The cavity slides out like a drawer on guide rails, with no hinge swing.

ideas.rationale: A pull-out drawer matches how people already open kitchen storage, so it needs no instruction.

ideas.title: Lift-Lid Clamshell

new_nodes.label: Top-lift gas-strut lid
new_nodes.detail: The entire top lifts like a toaster lid, held up by gas struts.

ideas.rationale: Lifting a lid is an action everyone performs without thinking, so no door logic is needed.

ideas.title: Magnetic Snap Door

new_nodes.label: Magnetic seal-latch
new_nodes.detail: Strong magnets hold the door and act as the safety switch, with no mechanical latch.

ideas.rationale: The door closes with a satisfying snap and cannot be closed wrongly.

ideas.title: Stirrer Replaces Turntable

new_nodes.label: Rotating metal mode stirrer
new_nodes.detail: A metal fan blade in the ceiling scatters microwaves, removing the need for a rotating plate.

ideas.rationale: Nothing needs to be placed on a turning tray, so the user cannot load it wrongly.

ideas.title: Ceramic Liner Cavity

new_nodes.label: Flat ceramic floor plate
new_nodes.detail: A flat ceramic plate with no tray or ring replaces the turntable assembly.

ideas.rationale: A plain flat floor is the easiest surface to wipe and needs no reloading of a tray.

ideas.title: Solid-State Power Amplifier

new_nodes.label: Solid-state GaN RF amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Transistor RF amplifiers replace the magnetron, transformer and high-voltage stack.

ideas.rationale: Instant on and off with no warm-up means the appliance behaves as the user expects.

ideas.title: Continuous Power Dial

new_nodes.label: Smooth analogue power slider
new_nodes.detail: A slider gives continuous power with no on/off cycling to understand.

ideas.rationale: A single continuous slider works like a light dimmer, which people already understand.

ideas.title: Low-Voltage Battery Pack Base

new_nodes.label: Docking battery base
new_nodes.detail: A rechargeable base powers the unit in short bursts, plugged in and charged overnight.

ideas.rationale: A single base with no cord means no plugging-in mistakes and no regional voltage confusion.

ideas.title: Magnetic Snap Power Base

new_nodes.label: Magnetic power puck
new_nodes.detail: The cord clicks onto the unit with a magnet, so it connects only one way.

ideas.rationale: A cord that cannot be inserted wrongly removes a common point of confusion.

ideas.title: Self-Resetting Fuse

new_nodes.label: Resettable polymer PTC fuse
new_nodes.detail: A polymer fuse resets itself once the fault clears, so no replacement is needed.

ideas.rationale: The unit recovers after a fault with no fuse to find or replace.

ideas.title: Infrared Food Reader

new_nodes.label: Infrared thermopile surface reader
new_nodes.detail: An infrared sensor reads the food surface temperature and ends cooking when it is hot.

ideas.rationale: The machine finishes the job by itself, so the user does not have to judge when food is ready.

ideas.title: Magnetic Reed Interlocks

new_nodes.label: Hall-effect door sensor
new_nodes.detail: A solid-state magnetic sensor replaces the three mechanical interlock switches.

ideas.rationale: A sensor with no moving parts works quietly and needs no adjustment or service by the user.

ideas.title: Passive Heat-Pipe Cooling

new_nodes.label: Heat-pipe fin cooler
new_nodes.detail: Sealed heat pipes move heat from the magnetron to outside fins with no fan.

ideas.rationale: Silent operation with no fan noise removes an unexplained sound that worries users.

ideas.title: Ceramic Fuse-Free Cutoff

new_nodes.label: Smart integrated protection chip
new_nodes.detail: One chip handles overcurrent and overheat protection and shows a single status light.

ideas.rationale: One unit that protects everything means nothing needs checking by the user.

ideas.title: Mica-Free Silicone Film

new_nodes.label: Disposable silicone splash film
new_nodes.detail: A cheap clip-in silicone sheet over the waveguide that is replaced when stained.

ideas.rationale: A simple clip-in sheet is easier to swap than a fragile mica plate that needs careful cleaning.

ideas.title: Self-Clean Cavity Coating

new_nodes.label: Photocatalytic cavity coating
new_nodes.detail: A coating breaks down food residue under the light of normal kitchen lighting.

ideas.rationale: Nothing needs scrubbing, so no cleaning routine has to be learned.

ideas.title: Dishwasher Cavity Liner

new_nodes.label: Removable cavity liner sleeve
new_nodes.detail: A clip-in metal-free liner slides out and goes into the dishwasher.

ideas.rationale: Taking out one simple liner is a single familiar action for cleaning.

ideas.title: Molded Fibre Wrapper

new_nodes.label: Metallised moulded-fibre shell
new_nodes.detail: A moulded fibre shell with a metal-coated inner layer forms the outer housing.

ideas.rationale: A light, cool-to-touch shell is less alarming and easier to handle for everyone.

ideas.title: Soft-Touch Fabric Skin

new_nodes.label: Removable fabric skin
new_nodes.detail: A washable soft cover slips over the body and carries the printed control icons.

ideas.rationale: A cover that can be changed in colour and feel makes the machine less intimidating.

ideas.title: Single Flat Glass Panel

new_nodes.label: Flat touch-glass pictogram panel
new_nodes.detail: A flat glass face shows three large pictograms for cook, reheat and defrost.

ideas.rationale: Three pictograms replace a crowded panel, so the choice is obvious at a glance.

ideas.title: Projected Countdown Ring

new_nodes.label: Floor-projected countdown ring
new_nodes.detail: A light ring projected onto the turntable floor shrinks as cooking progresses.

ideas.rationale: A shrinking ring on the floor shows time left in a way anyone can understand.

ideas.title: Gesture Wave Start

new_nodes.label: Hand-wave motion sensor
new_nodes.detail: A sensor above the door starts cooking when a hand is waved across the front.

ideas.rationale: A wave is an intuitive gesture that removes any need to find buttons.

ideas.title: Phone Tap Setup

new_nodes.label: NFC tap-to-cook tag
new_nodes.detail: Tap the food package on the unit and it reads cooking settings from the label.

ideas.rationale: Settings come from the food package, so the user never enters numbers.

ideas.title: Food Package Lid Reader

new_nodes.label: Barcode window in cavity roof
new_nodes.detail: A scanner reads a barcode printed on the meal tray and loads its cooking profile.

ideas.rationale: Scanning the packet is the only step, so no cooking knowledge is needed.

ideas.title: Auto Defrost by Touch

new_nodes.label: Single defrost plate sensor
new_nodes.detail: A plate sensor detects frozen food weight and runs a defrost cycle with no user input.

ideas.rationale: A defrost setting that chooses itself removes the need to know power and time for frozen food.

ideas.title: Butter Melt Pocket

new_nodes.label: Melt-only tray insert
new_nodes.detail: A shallow insert with a fixed low-power melt program for butter and chocolate.

ideas.rationale: A single insert with one fixed job removes every setting for the task.

ideas.title: Breakfast Drink Button

new_nodes.label: Single drink-warm button
new_nodes.detail: One large button warms a cup of drink to the right heat without any settings.

ideas.rationale: A one-press drink warm is the simplest breakfast action possible.

ideas.title: Recipe Card Cooking Mat

new_nodes.label: Printed recipe mat
new_nodes.detail: A flat mat placed under the dish shows its own pictured instructions and colour strips.

ideas.rationale: The mat carries the instructions with the food, so the machine needs no instructions of its own.

ideas.title: Cooking Sound Cue

new_nodes.label: Rhythmic sound progress tone
new_nodes.detail: A steady rhythmic tone speeds up as food nears done, signalling progress by ear.

ideas.rationale: Users can tell how far along the cooking is without looking or reading.

ideas.title: Stackable Mini Cooker

new_nodes.label: Stackable cavity module
new_nodes.detail: Small modular cavities stack on top of each other, sharing one control head.

ideas.rationale: Adding cavities as needed keeps each one simple to use while saving counter space.

ideas.title: Wall-Mounted Hob Unit

new_nodes.label: Wall-mounted flat cavity
new_nodes.detail: A flat unit fixes to the wall at eye height, with a door that opens at the same height as a cupboard.

ideas.rationale: Placing the unit at comfortable height removes bending and lifting for elderly users.

ideas.title: Fold-Down Shelf Microwave

new_nodes.label: Fold-down door shelf
new_nodes.detail: The door folds down into a shelf that doubles as the tray and the front cover.

ideas.rationale: The door becomes a shelf for the dish, so the user places food on a surface they already know.

ideas.title: Rounded Edge Cavity Mouth

new_nodes.label: Soft-edged cavity mouth
new_nodes.detail: A soft rubber lip around the opening makes the cavity safe to touch and reach.

ideas.rationale: Soft edges make the cavity hard to hurt yourself on, so no caution is needed when loading.

ideas.title: Shape-Matching Cavity Tray

new_nodes.label: Shaped cradle tray
new_nodes.detail: A cradle tray has moulded slots that match the common food container shapes.

ideas.rationale: Food sits in the right place by its own shape, so no positioning is needed.

ideas.title: Colour-Coded Power Wheel

new_nodes.label: Colour-band power wheel
new_nodes.detail: A wheel with four colour bands from pale to deep orange sets power by colour intensity.

ideas.rationale: Colour intensity maps naturally to heat, so no numbers need to be understood.

ideas.title: Hourglass Heat Level

new_nodes.label: Heat-density bar display
new_nodes.detail: A bar fills up to show how much heat the cavity is receiving.

ideas.rationale: A visible fill level tells the user the current power without any setting to learn.

ideas.title: Egg-Timer Mechanical Cam

new_nodes.label: Spring-wound egg-timer dial
new_nodes.detail: A classic egg-timer spring dial with a bell that rings at the end.

ideas.rationale: Users already know how to turn a timer dial and hear it ring.

ideas.title: Reheat Pizza Button

new_nodes.label: Dish-named reheat keys
new_nodes.detail: Keys are labelled with dish names such as pizza, rice and coffee, each with its own preset.

ideas.rationale: Named dish keys replace unknown numbers with words people already use.

ideas.title: Two-Hand Clap Start

new_nodes.label: Sound-activated start sensor
new_nodes.detail: A microphone responds to a clap or a spoken word to start the unit.

ideas.rationale: A clap or spoken word is accessible for people who cannot easily press small buttons.

ideas.title: Sealed Membrane Keypad

new_nodes.label: Flush sealed membrane panel
new_nodes.detail: A flat, sealed panel with raised bumps shows one big start key and no gaps to clean.
