ideas.title: Superheat-Proof Vessel Lid

new_nodes.label: Boil-safe mug with air-entry
new_nodes.detail: A mug with a perforated insert prevents superheating and eruptive boiling.

ideas.rationale: A drink can be heated without the user knowing the physics of superheating, so there is no hazard to manage.

ideas.title: Hot-Drink Button

new_nodes.label: One-touch hot drink
new_nodes.detail: A single labelled button heats a drink to the right temperature without any timing.

ideas.rationale: A breakfast drink becomes one labelled press, so even someone half awake can use it correctly.

ideas.title: Smell-to-Pause Guard

new_nodes.label: Arc-detect camera stop
new_nodes.detail: A small camera and arc sensor pauses cooking if metal sparks, and it explains the problem in plain words.

ideas.rationale: Mistakes like metal in the cavity are caught and explained, so the user does not have to remember the rules.

ideas.title: Voice Says It, Oven Does It

new_nodes.label: On-device speech command module
new_nodes.detail: Hears plain phrases like 'warm my soup for two minutes' and sets the timer.

new_nodes.label: Offline speech recognition
new_nodes.detail: Small neural model runs on a low-cost microcontroller with no cloud link.

ideas.rationale: Speaking a request in ordinary words needs no dial, numbers or manual, so an elderly user can start cooking immediately.

ideas.title: Food Icon Dial

new_nodes.label: Picture dial with food icons
new_nodes.detail: Single dial showing soup, rice, pizza, leftovers, each pre-setting time and power.

ideas.rationale: Choosing a picture of the food removes the need to understand minutes, percentages or power levels.

ideas.title: One Press Cooks Whatever Is Inside

new_nodes.label: Infrared food-surface scanner
new_nodes.detail: Reads temperature and moisture of the food and sets time and power automatically.

new_nodes.label: Thermal-image food classification
new_nodes.detail: Low-resolution IR array maps heat and classifies the load.

ideas.rationale: A single START button with automatic settings means the user never has to make a choice at all.

ideas.title: Hourglass Starter

new_nodes.label: Flip-to-start sand hourglass
new_nodes.detail: Flipping the hourglass starts heating; sand running out ends it.

ideas.rationale: Flipping a visible sand timer is an action anyone already understands, so no numbers or settings are needed.

ideas.title: Plate Puck Timer

new_nodes.label: Cooking puck on plate
new_nodes.detail: A coin-sized puck placed on the plate sets the time from its colour and mass.

ideas.rationale: Placing the food on a plate with a puck on it removes both the timer knob and the need to know any times.

ideas.title: Transparent Conductive Door

new_nodes.label: ITO-coated glass door panel
new_nodes.detail: Indium tin oxide coating blocks microwaves while staying fully clear.

new_nodes.label: Transparent conductive coating
new_nodes.detail: Thin conductive film on glass that reflects RF but passes visible light.

ideas.rationale: A fully clear door lets the user see the food without any mesh, which reduces confusion about whether anything is happening.

ideas.title: Glowing Cavity Walls

new_nodes.label: Edge-lit light guide frame
new_nodes.detail: LED ring around the door sends light through the glass and lights the cavity from outside.

ideas.rationale: Lighting the cavity from outside removes the interior bulb and its failure point, keeping the food visible with no extra steps.

ideas.title: Door Turns Colour When Done

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic door window ring
new_nodes.detail: Ring around the window changes colour when the cavity reaches serving temperature.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic pigment
new_nodes.detail: Colour-changing ink reacts to heat without power or electronics.

ideas.rationale: A colour change on the window signals completion without any numbers or bells, so the user knows when to stop.

ideas.title: Heat Level as Colour Bar

new_nodes.label: Touch colour bar
new_nodes.detail: Tap anywhere on a bar from cool blue to red hot; the position sets power.

ideas.rationale: Colours map intuitively to heat, so the user does not need to read a numbered power scale.

ideas.title: Two Buttons Only

new_nodes.label: Warm and Hot buttons
new_nodes.detail: Two large buttons select pre-set duty cycles for reheating and cooking.

ideas.rationale: Reducing five power steps to two clear words removes the choice that causes most confusion.

ideas.title: Auto Power by Feel

new_nodes.label: Adaptive duty-cycle controller
new_nodes.detail: Chooses the on/off ratio automatically from the food's heat response.

ideas.rationale: Letting the machine pick the power means the user never sees or touches a power setting.

ideas.title: Squeeze to Heat

new_nodes.label: Pressure-sensing front plate
new_nodes.detail: Pressing harder on the front panel increases power and time, releasing stops.

ideas.rationale: Pushing harder to cook and letting go to stop is a direct physical action that needs no reading or learning.

ideas.title: Doneness Ring Light

new_nodes.label: Ring light countdown
new_nodes.detail: Light ring around the door slowly shrinks to nothing when cooking is complete.

ideas.rationale: A shrinking ring shows time left at a glance, which avoids the imprecise mechanical timer entirely.

ideas.title: Bell Becomes Door Pop

new_nodes.label: Spring-assisted door pop
new_nodes.detail: When cooking ends, the door springs open a few centimetres to signal completion.

ideas.rationale: The door itself announces that the food is ready, so no bell or number is needed to understand the machine's state.

ideas.title: Haptic Handle Alert

new_nodes.label: Vibrating door handle
new_nodes.detail: Handle buzzes softly in the hand when cooking ends.

ideas.rationale: A buzz in the hand is noticed even by users with poor hearing or sight, so they know when to open the door.

ideas.title: Door Opens on Its Own

new_nodes.label: Motorised auto-release latch
new_nodes.detail: Latch releases automatically when cooking stops, with no button to press.

ideas.rationale: The door opens by itself when cooking ends, so there is nothing to find or press at the end.

ideas.title: Handle as Button

new_nodes.label: Pull-to-open handle
new_nodes.detail: A large handle that opens the door when pulled, with no separate release button.

ideas.rationale: A handle that is pulled is more obvious than a small button to find and press.

ideas.title: Magnet Door Latch

new_nodes.label: Neodymium magnetic latch
new_nodes.detail: Magnet holds the door shut and releases with a firm pull, no levers needed.

ideas.rationale: A magnetic catch has no button or lever to learn, so the door simply closes and opens by feel.

ideas.title: Sliding Drawer Door

new_nodes.label: Sliding glass drawer door
new_nodes.detail: Door slides sideways on rails, needing no hinges or swing clearance.

ideas.rationale: A sliding door moves in a single obvious direction and never swings into the user's arm.

ideas.title: Lift-Up Lid Oven

new_nodes.label: Gas-spring lift lid
new_nodes.detail: Top-opening lid lifts with a gas spring, so the user simply lifts it like a box.

ideas.rationale: Lifting a lid is an everyday action, and the gas spring means an elderly user needs almost no force.

ideas.title: Floating Magnetic Hinge

new_nodes.label: Magnetic floating hinge
new_nodes.detail: Door floats on magnets, closing gently and staying where put.

ideas.rationale: A door that stays where it is put removes the need to hold it open or fight it closed.

ideas.title: Plastic Living Hinge

new_nodes.label: Moulded living hinge
new_nodes.detail: Hinge moulded in one piece from polypropylene, no welding or fasteners.

ideas.rationale: A one-piece moulded hinge is cheaper to make and has fewer parts that can break or confuse.

ideas.title: Moulded Cavity Not Steel

new_nodes.label: Laser-direct-structured plastic cavity
new_nodes.detail: Plastic cavity with a laser-patterned metal layer that shields the microwaves.

ideas.rationale: A lighter, cheaper cavity that is easier to clean makes the machine less intimidating to pick up and wipe down.

ideas.title: Cavity Mirrors Visible Light Only

new_nodes.label: Dichroic cavity coating
new_nodes.detail: Coating reflects microwaves and passes visible light, serving the window function without holes.

ideas.rationale: Removing the perforated mesh makes the door look simple, with the food clearly visible.

ideas.title: Remove the Turntable

new_nodes.label: Built-in mode stirrer
new_nodes.detail: Field stirrer evens out heat so the food sits still on a flat tray.

ideas.rationale: With no turntable to lift out and reposition, cleaning and loading involve fewer steps.

ideas.title: Shelf That Comes to You

new_nodes.label: Motorised pull-in tray
new_nodes.detail: Tray slides out at waist height when the user taps it, then pulls back in to cook.

ideas.rationale: Bringing the food to the user at a comfortable height means no bending, reaching or lifting heavy plates.

ideas.title: Food Goes In on Its Own

new_nodes.label: Conveyor drop-in slot
new_nodes.detail: Place food on a slot and it is drawn into the cavity and cooked.

ideas.rationale: Loading becomes one motion with no door to open, so there is nothing to misunderstand.

ideas.title: Packaging Sets the Oven

new_nodes.label: Package NFC tag reader
new_nodes.detail: Reads a tag printed on food packaging and sets time and power automatically.

new_nodes.label: Passive NFC tags
new_nodes.detail: Printed tags carry cooking instructions with no battery.

ideas.rationale: Tapping the packet to the oven lets the food itself supply every setting, so the user chooses nothing.

ideas.title: Card Cook

new_nodes.label: Picture card slot
new_nodes.detail: Insert a wallet-sized card with a food picture and the machine cooks it.

ideas.rationale: A printed card with a picture is simple, cheap and makes choosing a recipe a physical, visual act.

ideas.title: Mains Plug That Fits Anywhere

new_nodes.label: Auto-voltage power supply
new_nodes.detail: Accepts 100-240 V at 50 or 60 Hz, so one model works everywhere.

ideas.rationale: One model for every mains supply means no confusion about buying or setting the right machine.

ideas.title: Shaped Plate Sets Time

new_nodes.label: Depth-sensing cavity floor
new_nodes.detail: Sensor under the tray measures the food depth and sets time from it.

ideas.rationale: Measuring the food's own size sets the time, so the user does not guess a number.

ideas.title: Sound of Popping Ends It

new_nodes.label: Acoustic doneness sensor
new_nodes.detail: Microphone hears popcorn popping or sizzling stop and ends cooking.

new_nodes.label: Audio event detection
new_nodes.detail: Simple sound classifier listens for change in cooking noise.

ideas.rationale: Stopping when the food's natural sound changes requires no judgment, just letting the food speak.

ideas.title: Thermal Fuse Plate

new_nodes.label: Self-stopping heat plate
new_nodes.detail: Plate contains a bimetal disc that cuts power when the food reaches serving temperature.

ideas.rationale: A plate that stops heating by itself removes the need for any timer or setting at all.

ideas.title: One Dial Does Everything

new_nodes.label: Single rotary icon dial
new_nodes.detail: One dial with icons from light to hot; turning it sets both time and power.

ideas.rationale: Merging two controls into one physical dial halves what the user must understand.

ideas.title: Wave to Start

new_nodes.label: Gesture sensor panel
new_nodes.detail: Hand wave up or down adjusts the setting; a flat palm starts or stops.

new_nodes.label: Infrared gesture recognition
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost IR sensor detects hand motion without touching.

ideas.rationale: Waving a hand is a natural gesture with no button to find and no reading required.

ideas.title: Hand Over the Food

new_nodes.label: Touchless hand-hover start
new_nodes.detail: Hover a hand over the oven, which begins cooking; withdraw to pause.

ideas.rationale: Hovering to start and withdrawing to stop is intuitive and needs no touching of a greasy panel.

ideas.title: Printed Recipe Dial Cover

new_nodes.label: Recipe cover with cut-outs
new_nodes.detail: Clear cover over the dial shows only a few large pictures for the common dishes.

ideas.rationale: Showing only a handful of large, obvious choices removes clutter for users who find small labels hard to read.

ideas.title: Slow Cooker Mode Only

new_nodes.label: Long gentle cook preset
new_nodes.detail: Single preset cooks slowly at low duty for an hour, for any dish.

ideas.rationale: One forgiving preset that heats gently makes it hard to burn food by picking the wrong level.

ideas.title: Two Doors, One Action

new_nodes.label: Front-access door with open-plate
new_nodes.detail: Door opens fully when you press one wide plate, no latch or button.

ideas.rationale: A large wide plate is easier to hit than a small button, which helps users with limited dexterity.

ideas.title: Elbow Press Opening

new_nodes.label: Broad soft-touch door plate
new_nodes.detail: Wide cushioned plate that opens the door when pressed with any part of the body.

ideas.rationale: Accepting a press with any body part means a user with arthritis or full hands can still open the door.

ideas.title: Door Closes Itself

new_nodes.label: Soft-close damper hinge
new_nodes.detail: Door is pushed near shut and the damper draws it closed with a gentle sound.

ideas.rationale: A door that closes itself once nudged means the user never has to remember to shut it properly.

ideas.title: Magnetic Snap Lock Done

new_nodes.label: Interlock magnet sensor
new_nodes.detail: Magnet sensor makes sure the door is shut before power is allowed, with no user step.

ideas.rationale: The machine checks the door itself, so the user never needs to think about safety settings.

ideas.title: Ambient Scent Done Signal

new_nodes.label: Warm-aroma cue
new_nodes.detail: Gentle warm scent is released when cooking reaches the target temperature.

ideas.rationale: Smelling that food is ready is a natural signal that needs no reading, number or sound.

ideas.title: Snapping Fingers Starts It

new_nodes.label: Clap-to-start microphone
new_nodes.detail: Two claps or a snap start cooking; a silence after the bell stops it.

ideas.rationale: A clap is an action anyone can make, so it removes both the timer and the door button from the learning curve.

ideas.title: Plug-and-Play Recipe Pad

new_nodes.label: Phone-linked recipe scan
new_nodes.detail: Phone camera scans food; the oven sets itself through a single shared app.

ideas.rationale: Pointing a phone at the food removes the need for any settings on the oven itself.

ideas.title: Oven Speaks Your Language

new_nodes.label: Spoken prompt speaker
new_nodes.detail: Speaks short plain prompts like 'Put food in, press start' in the user's language.

ideas.rationale: Spoken instructions in the user's own language remove the need to read a manual or any on-panel text.

ideas.title: Retro Cooker With Only a Bell

new_nodes.label: Single sprung timer lever
new_nodes.detail: One lever wound by hand; cooking runs for a set fixed turn of the lever.

ideas.rationale: A single lever with a fixed turn is the simplest possible timer, removing any choice of minutes.

ideas.title: Tray Heats Food Only

new_nodes.label: Induction heat tray
new_nodes.detail: Tray heats the food directly through induction, so the cavity barely warms.

ideas.rationale: Heating only the food with a tray that sets its own power removes the need to adjust the oven's power at all.

ideas.title: Shape-Coded Buttons

new_nodes.label: Tactile shape-coded buttons
new_nodes.detail: Each button has a unique shape so it can be found by touch without looking.

ideas.rationale: Shape-coded buttons can be used by touch alone, which suits elderly users who cannot see small labels well.

ideas.title: Two-Tone Sound Done

new_nodes.label: Rising two-tone chime
new_nodes.detail: A distinct pleasant chime plays when cooking is finished, repeating until the door is opened.

ideas.rationale: A repeating chime keeps signalling until the user responds, so nobody misses that the food is ready.

ideas.title: Food Tells You It Is Hot

new_nodes.label: Serving-temperature LED
new_nodes.detail: Small light on the plate glows green when the food is at serving temperature.

ideas.rationale: A simple green light on the plate shows readiness with no reading and no guessing.

ideas.title: Microwave Becomes a Drawer

new_nodes.label: Under-counter pull-out cavity
new_nodes.detail: Cavity pulls out like a drawer, with no door, hinges or latch at all.

ideas.rationale: A pull-out drawer uses the familiar motion of opening a kitchen drawer and needs no separate door action.

ideas.title: Single Hungry Button

new_nodes.label: VOC gas sensor array
new_nodes.detail: Detects steam and aroma to estimate food state.

new_nodes.label: Auto-selects heating time and power
new_nodes.detail: Removes manual timer and power setting.

ideas.rationale: One button that cooks by sensing the food removes every setting the user must learn.

ideas.title: Weight-Sensing Cavity Floor

new_nodes.label: Load-cell cavity floor
new_nodes.detail: Measures food mass and sets energy automatically.

ideas.rationale: Placing food on the floor is the only action needed, because mass sets the cooking profile.

ideas.title: Silhouette Presets

new_nodes.label: Tactile silhouette keypad
new_nodes.detail: Raised icons of mug, bowl and plate.

ideas.rationale: Users pick a picture of their container and the machine handles the rest.

ideas.title: Door Opens on Approach

new_nodes.label: Capacitive proximity sensor door
new_nodes.detail: Door swings open when a hand nears the handle.

ideas.rationale: No button to find or press means the door works the way a fridge door does.

ideas.title: Photoluminescent Glow Cavity

new_nodes.label: Photoluminescent cavity paint
new_nodes.detail: Stores light from the room and glows without power or heat.

ideas.rationale: The cavity stays visible for food checking with no bulb to switch on or manage.

ideas.title: Solid-State Cooking Without Magnetron

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Generates 2.45 GHz energy at low voltage.

ideas.rationale: Removing the high-voltage stage removes the parts that make the machine intimidating and dangerous.

ideas.title: Zero Stored Charge Design

new_nodes.label: Stores no energy after switch-off
new_nodes.detail: No capacitor holds charge, so nothing needs discharging.

ideas.rationale: Users never worry about a lethal charge, so the machine needs no caution around it.

ideas.title: Battery Pack Oven

new_nodes.label: Swappable battery pack
new_nodes.detail: Rechargeable pack powers the RF stage.

ideas.rationale: With no cord or outlet to find, the machine can sit anywhere without setup.

ideas.title: Wall Magnetic Cord Snap

new_nodes.label: Magnetic plug dock
new_nodes.detail: Plug snaps to a wall dock with alignment built in.

ideas.rationale: The plug connects by proximity, so a user cannot connect it wrongly.

ideas.title: Induction Puck Base

new_nodes.label: Inductive power puck
new_nodes.detail: Oven sits on a puck that powers it with no plug.

ideas.rationale: Placing the oven on the puck is the entire setup, with no wires to think about.

ideas.title: Auto-Eject Door Done Signal

new_nodes.label: Physical done signal
new_nodes.detail: Door cracks open a few millimetres when cooking ends.

ideas.rationale: Opening the door is the notification, so no sound or light needs interpreting.

ideas.title: Scent Done Alert

new_nodes.label: Aroma cartridge emitter
new_nodes.detail: Releases a pleasant smell when cooking finishes.

ideas.rationale: A familiar smell tells anyone the food is ready without reading anything.

ideas.title: Turntable Nudge Alert

new_nodes.label: Tactile done alert
new_nodes.detail: Turntable rocks briefly when cooking ends.

ideas.rationale: Motion replaces the bell, so the signal works for users who cannot hear.

ideas.title: Rotating Antenna Replaces Turntable

new_nodes.label: Rotating RF mode stirrer
new_nodes.detail: Spins the field inside a fixed cavity.

ideas.rationale: Food heats evenly without being placed on a turning plate, so no alignment is needed.

ideas.title: Self-Centering Cavity

new_nodes.label: Cavity with no fixed floor
new_nodes.detail: Food sits anywhere and the field adapts.

ideas.rationale: Users stop thinking about where food goes because placement no longer matters.

ideas.title: Air Curtain Door Seal

new_nodes.label: Air knife seal
new_nodes.detail: A curtain of airflow blocks microwave leakage.

ideas.rationale: No rubber rim to clean or misalign means the door stays easy to maintain.

ideas.title: Magnetic Self-Sealing Door

new_nodes.label: Magnetic gasket
new_nodes.detail: Magnets pull the door shut and seal it.

ideas.rationale: The door closes itself, so it cannot be left open by mistake.

ideas.title: Single Hall Sensor Interlock

new_nodes.label: Hall-effect door sensor
new_nodes.detail: One magnetic sensor confirms the door is closed.

ideas.rationale: A simpler sensor reduces faults and fewer parts means fewer ways to fail.

ideas.title: PTC Self-Resetting Thermal Fuse

new_nodes.label: PTC polymer thermal fuse
new_nodes.detail: Resets itself after cooling without any user action.

ideas.rationale: Overheat trips heal themselves, so users never have to reset anything.

ideas.title: Infrared Food Thermometer Stop

new_nodes.label: Infrared thermopile sensor
new_nodes.detail: Reads food surface temperature without contact.

ideas.rationale: The machine stops when food is hot, so overcooking is no longer the user's problem.

ideas.title: Sound Feedback Cavity

new_nodes.label: Acoustic food sensing
new_nodes.detail: Listens to sizzle and steam to judge doneness.

ideas.rationale: The oven listens to food, so the user only has to put it in.

ideas.title: Voice Food Name Command

new_nodes.label: Local speech recognizer
new_nodes.detail: Accepts simple food names offline.

ideas.rationale: Users say the food name, which needs no manual or menu knowledge.

ideas.title: Barcode Auto-Program

new_nodes.label: Packaging code reader
new_nodes.detail: Reads a code printed on the food package.

ideas.rationale: Scanning the package sets the program, so the user does not choose settings.

ideas.title: NFC Tap-to-Cook Plate

new_nodes.label: NFC food tag
new_nodes.detail: Tag on a plate or packet sets the cooking profile.

ideas.rationale: Touching the food to the oven gives it the instructions it needs.

ideas.title: Door Tap Opens Drawer

new_nodes.label: Spring drawer mechanism
new_nodes.detail: Drawer slides out after a light tap.

ideas.rationale: A tap opens the drawer, which is a motion everyone already knows.

ideas.title: Built-In Drawer Microwave

new_nodes.label: Cabinet-integrated drawer
new_nodes.detail: Oven built into a kitchen cabinet.

ideas.rationale: Built into the kitchen, the oven needs no counter space or setup.

ideas.title: Compostable Splatter Liner

new_nodes.label: Disposable splatter sleeve
new_nodes.detail: Thin cover that is thrown away after use.

ideas.rationale: Users replace a sleeve instead of cleaning, so there is no maintenance to learn.

ideas.title: Self-Healing Silicone Cover

new_nodes.label: Self-healing silicone laminate
new_nodes.detail: Cover that seals small cuts and scratches.

ideas.rationale: A cover that repairs itself never needs replacing or careful handling.

ideas.title: Printed Pictogram Floor

new_nodes.label: Pictogram glass turntable
new_nodes.detail: Turntable printed with food icons and placement marks.

ideas.rationale: Visual placement marks show where food goes without reading a manual.

ideas.title: Glass-Free Screen Door

new_nodes.label: Door touchscreen
new_nodes.detail: Shows a live camera image of the cavity.

ideas.rationale: A live picture replaces the window, so users see the food without any settings.

ideas.title: Live Camera Window

new_nodes.label: Cavity camera
new_nodes.detail: Small camera inside sends an image to the door display.

ideas.rationale: Users see inside on any display, so the window and its glass are no longer needed.

ideas.title: Metal Detection Lockout

new_nodes.label: Metal presence camera
new_nodes.detail: Detects metal objects and refuses to start.

ideas.rationale: The oven blocks mistakes so users never have to remember which materials are safe.

ideas.title: Bubble Breaker Turntable Pulse

new_nodes.label: Vibration bubble prevention
new_nodes.detail: Brief vibration breaks up superheated liquid.

ideas.rationale: The machine handles eruptive boiling so users need no special technique for drinks.

ideas.title: Auto Liquid Mode

new_nodes.label: Automatic liquid detection
new_nodes.detail: Detects liquid and adjusts power and time.

ideas.rationale: Users stop choosing liquid settings because the oven recognises the contents.

ideas.title: Electroluminescent Cavity Walls

new_nodes.label: Electroluminescent film
new_nodes.detail: Thin film glows evenly with no heat.

ideas.rationale: Even, cool light makes the cavity easy to see without any bulb.

ideas.title: Ambient Light Ring Status

new_nodes.label: Colour status indicator
new_nodes.detail: Light ring shows heating, ready and standby.

ideas.rationale: A colour code is understood at a glance, so no manual is required.

ideas.title: Dial-Free Single Wheel Control

new_nodes.label: Single detent wheel
new_nodes.detail: One wheel with three labelled positions.

ideas.rationale: Three positions replace many settings, so the control is easy to learn.

ideas.title: Power Cam Replaced By Software

new_nodes.label: Software duty-cycle control
new_nodes.detail: Firmware sets average power automatically.

ideas.rationale: Software sets power levels, so the user does not turn any mechanism.

ideas.title: Mechanical Timer Replaced By Clock Glance

new_nodes.label: Digital countdown display
new_nodes.detail: Shows remaining time in large numbers.

ideas.rationale: A clear readout is easier to understand than a dial that is hard to set precisely.

ideas.title: Thermal Camera Auto Mode

new_nodes.label: Thermal imaging array
new_nodes.detail: Maps food temperature across the cavity.

ideas.rationale: The oven sees whether food is hot, so the user needs no judgement.

ideas.title: Voice-Free Gesture Start

new_nodes.label: Hand wave sensor
new_nodes.detail: Waving over the front starts or stops cooking.

ideas.rationale: Waving is intuitive and works even with messy or wet hands.

ideas.title: Tilt-To-Start Tray

new_nodes.label: Tilt sensor base
new_nodes.detail: Tilting the tray starts cooking.

ideas.rationale: Moving the tray is a natural action that starts cooking without any buttons.

ideas.title: Self-Cleaning Cavity Coating

new_nodes.label: Catalytic self-cleaning coating
new_nodes.detail: Breaks down food spots at heat.

ideas.rationale: The cavity cleans itself, so users never need to learn a cleaning routine.

ideas.title: Modular Snap Cavity Tray

new_nodes.label: Snap-fit modular tray
new_nodes.detail: Tray clips in only one correct way.

ideas.rationale: A keyed tray cannot be fitted wrongly, which removes assembly confusion.

ideas.title: Stick-On Instruction Surface

new_nodes.label: Single iconic front panel
new_nodes.detail: One image shows how to start.

ideas.rationale: A single picture replaces the instruction manual, so no reading is needed.

ideas.title: Preloaded Meal Capsule

new_nodes.label: Meal capsule reader
new_nodes.detail: Reads a pre-sealed meal pack and runs its program.

ideas.rationale: Pressing a sealed meal into the oven is the only step needed to cook it.

ideas.title: Subscription Auto Reheat

new_nodes.label: Remote program download
new_nodes.detail: Cooking programs arrive from the cloud.

ideas.rationale: The oven learns the right settings remotely so a student never has to figure them out.

ideas.title: Plate-Shaped Oven Cavity

new_nodes.label: Flat plate cavity
new_nodes.detail: Shallow cavity holds one plate at a time.

ideas.rationale: A flat cavity makes placement obvious for any user, since the plate is the only space.

ideas.title: Hot Plate Replaces Oven Box

new_nodes.label: Resonant ceramic hotplate
new_nodes.detail: Heats food from a flat surface.

ideas.rationale: A flat surface needs no door, cavity or settings, so it is simpler to use.

ideas.title: Wearable Cook Reminder

new_nodes.label: Wristband done alert
new_nodes.detail: Vibrates when food is ready.

ideas.rationale: Students can leave the kitchen and still know when food is ready.

ideas.title: Ceiling-Mounted Fold Oven

new_nodes.label: Under-cabinet lift mount
new_nodes.detail: Oven lifts out of cabinet space on demand.

ideas.rationale: Small kitchens can hide the oven, so students need no counter space to plan around.

ideas.title: Frozen Food Auto Thaw Lock

new_nodes.label: Automatic frozen food detection
new_nodes.detail: Detects frozen food and runs a thaw cycle.

ideas.rationale: The oven decides the cycle, so users never need to know about thawing times.

ideas.title: Crisp Lid Auto Mode

new_nodes.label: Hot air crisping plate
new_nodes.detail: Adds heat to brown the surface when needed.

ideas.rationale: Crisping happens automatically, so users do not need to choose browning modes.

ideas.title: Voice-Free Meal Menu Wall

new_nodes.label: Photo menu panel
new_nodes.detail: Shows large photos of common meals to tap.

ideas.rationale: Tapping a photo of the meal is the most direct way to cook for a new user.

ideas.title: Hourglass Timer Dial

new_nodes.label: Sand-drain hourglass timer
new_nodes.detail: A clear chamber of fine sand drains visibly; when empty, heating stops and a soft thud is heard.

ideas.rationale: Users read remaining time at a glance by watching sand, which needs no numbers, no dial calibration, and no learning.

ideas.title: Food-Photo Power Selector

new_nodes.label: Four-picture power pad
new_nodes.detail: Printed pictures of popcorn, leftovers, frozen meal and reheat drink replace the numbered 5-step knob.

ideas.rationale: Choosing by picture of the food removes the need to understand power levels or duty cycles.

ideas.title: Door Pull-to-Open Hinge

new_nodes.label: Spring-assisted pull door
new_nodes.detail: Door opens with a light tug on its edge; no push button required.

ideas.rationale: A door that opens the way any cupboard does removes the button that users must find and understand.

ideas.title: Glow-Film Door Window

new_nodes.label: Electroluminescent film
new_nodes.detail: A thin film on the door glass lights the cavity when the door is opened, at very low cost.

ideas.rationale: Interior visibility comes from a self-lit film that needs no bulb, socket or wiring, so there is nothing to switch or fail.

ideas.title: Inductive Wall Dock Power

new_nodes.label: Countertop inductive power pad
new_nodes.detail: The oven sits on a pad that transfers power wirelessly, so no plug or cord is needed.

ideas.rationale: Placing the oven on a pad is simpler than finding a socket and fitting a plug.

ideas.title: Tap-to-Start Single Surface

new_nodes.label: Single capacitive tap pad
new_nodes.detail: One flat touch area starts a standard reheat cycle; tapping again adds more time.

ideas.rationale: One tap with a sensible default means the user never needs to set anything at all.

ideas.title: Spoken Done Voice

new_nodes.label: Speech synthesis chip
new_nodes.detail: The oven speaks short phrases such as 'Your food is ready, open the door'.

ideas.rationale: Spoken instructions tell the user what to do next without any manual or icons.

ideas.title: Scent Done Alert

new_nodes.label: Scented cartridge release
new_nodes.detail: A small cartridge releases a warm popcorn scent when cooking finishes.

ideas.rationale: A pleasant smell signals that food is done, which is intuitive even for someone who has never used the oven.

ideas.title: NFC Meal Tag Autoprogram

new_nodes.label: NFC food-package tag
new_nodes.detail: A tag on each frozen meal tells the oven the power and time to use.

ideas.rationale: The user taps the packet on the oven and nothing else, so cooking settings never have to be known.

ideas.title: Weighing Tray Auto-Timer

new_nodes.label: Load-cell tray
new_nodes.detail: A weighing tray measures the food and sets time and power automatically.

ideas.rationale: The oven decides how long to cook from the weight of the food, so the user does not have to.

ideas.title: Hands-Free Gesture Start

new_nodes.label: Infrared proximity sensing
new_nodes.detail: Waving a hand near the front starts or stops heating.

ideas.rationale: A wave is a gesture everyone already knows, so no buttons need to be learned.

ideas.title: Portion Plate Sensor

new_nodes.label: Infrared food-surface camera
new_nodes.detail: A low-cost IR sensor reads the surface temperature and stops at the right point.

ideas.rationale: Stopping when the food is hot, not after a fixed time, means users cannot ruin a meal by guessing.

ideas.title: Cookbook-in-a-Cup

new_nodes.label: Boil-safe nucleation stick
new_nodes.detail: A disposable stick in the cup releases bubbles so liquid boils gently.

ideas.rationale: The stick removes the risk of eruptive boiling so users need no knowledge of superheating.

ideas.title: Foil Warning Camera

new_nodes.label: Cavity metal-detect camera
new_nodes.detail: A small camera spots foil or metal and shows a simple red icon with a spoken warning.

ideas.rationale: The oven tells the user what is wrong before it arcs, so no one needs to know the rule about metal.

ideas.title: Metal-Proof Cavity Lining

new_nodes.label: Arc-tolerant ceramic liner
new_nodes.detail: A ceramic liner resists arcing so small metal fragments are harmless.

ideas.rationale: Users can put in any dish without worrying about a warning or a spark.

ideas.title: Bleed-Resistor Discharge Pack

new_nodes.label: Passive bleed network
new_nodes.detail: A permanent resistor network drains the high-voltage store within seconds of switching off.

ideas.rationale: Cleaning or unplugging the oven becomes safe without any user action or knowledge.

ideas.title: Solid-State Gallium Heater

new_nodes.label: GaN RF amplifier
new_nodes.detail: A solid-state amplifier generates microwaves at low voltage, with no high-voltage diode stack.

ideas.rationale: Removing the high-voltage stack removes the lethal-charge hazard that makes microwaves intimidating.

ideas.title: Battery-Free Lunch Tote

new_nodes.label: Hot-stone tote
new_nodes.detail: A bag with a phase-change pack heats the food by itself when opened.

ideas.rationale: A student with no kitchen can heat a meal by opening a bag, with no oven at all.

ideas.title: Fold-Flat Silicone Mat Turntable

new_nodes.label: Flexible silicone food mat
new_nodes.detail: A silicone mat replaces the glass turntable and folds for storage.

ideas.rationale: A mat that can be put in a dishwasher and that cannot break makes cleaning obvious.

ideas.title: Stirrer-Fan Turntable Removal

new_nodes.label: Rotating waveguide stirrer
new_nodes.detail: A moving metal stirrer spreads the microwaves so the food heats evenly without a turntable.

ideas.rationale: With no turntable to load, the user only places food in the oven, and that is all there is to do.

ideas.title: Gravity-Shutter Safety

new_nodes.label: Gravity-closing RF shutter
new_nodes.detail: A metal shutter drops by gravity when the door opens, blocking microwave leakage.

ideas.rationale: A purely mechanical shutter is safe even if electronics fail, so users never have to trust a switch.

ideas.title: Magnet Latch Door

new_nodes.label: Magnetic door catch
new_nodes.detail: A strong magnet holds the door shut and releases it with a light push.

ideas.rationale: The door closes with a soft click and opens with a push, with no lever to find or understand.

ideas.title: Stove-Top Inspired Dial Only

new_nodes.label: Single hot-cold dial
new_nodes.detail: One dial runs from cold to hot, with no numbers or timer.

ideas.rationale: People already know a dial that goes from cold to hot, so no instruction is needed.

ideas.title: Motion Timer Coffee Jar

new_nodes.label: Clip-on seal gasket
new_nodes.detail: A snap-on gasket clips onto the door rim and needs no adjustment.

ideas.rationale: A seal that fits by itself removes maintenance and avoids any user decisions about it.

ideas.title: Self-Healing Door Seal

new_nodes.label: Self-healing elastomer
new_nodes.detail: A rubber-like material re-seals itself after small cuts or wear.

ideas.rationale: The seal keeps working for years without anyone noticing or having to replace it.

ideas.title: Sliding Drawer Oven

new_nodes.label: Sliding drawer door
new_nodes.detail: The whole front slides out like a drawer, with the food tray moving with it.

ideas.rationale: Pulling out a drawer to load food is the most familiar motion in any kitchen.

ideas.title: Lift-Lid Top Loader

new_nodes.label: Gas-strut lift lid
new_nodes.detail: The entire top lifts with a gas strut, so the user drops food in from above.

ideas.rationale: Putting a bowl in from above is as natural as using a bin, so no door handling is needed.

ideas.title: Doneness Chime Sound

new_nodes.label: Tonal ready-chime
new_nodes.detail: A rising two-note chime signals that food is ready, replacing the bell.

ideas.rationale: A pleasant rising chime is understood everywhere, so the user does not need to read anything.

ideas.title: Silent Peltier Cooling

new_nodes.label: Peltier cooling plate
new_nodes.detail: A solid-state cooler removes heat from the electronics with no fan.

ideas.rationale: A silent oven that does not hum or whir is calmer for a student sharing a flat.

ideas.title: Frozen-Meal Drive-Through Hatch

new_nodes.label: Single-action hatch
new_nodes.detail: A hatch in the side lets a meal slide in and out, with a single cycle that runs automatically.

ideas.rationale: A student can put a meal in and take it out with no decisions in between.

ideas.title: Shape-Sensing Auto Power

new_nodes.label: Dielectric food sensing
new_nodes.detail: The oven senses the water content of food and sets power on its own.

ideas.rationale: Power is set without any user choice, so there is nothing to misjudge.

ideas.title: Tilt-Up Glass Front

new_nodes.label: Fully glass front door
new_nodes.detail: The entire front is transparent glass that pivots up at the top.

ideas.rationale: A clear front that opens upward shows the food and the open action in one glance.

ideas.title: Auto-Door Light Curtain

new_nodes.label: Optical light-curtain interlock
new_nodes.detail: An infrared beam across the opening stops heating when an arm or object breaks it.

ideas.rationale: Safety happens automatically, so the user never has to think about a door switch.

ideas.title: Hourglass Chime Wizard

new_nodes.label: Browning-free crisp tray
new_nodes.detail: A preheated metal crisp tray browns the food surface without needing a grill.

ideas.rationale: Users get crisp results with one step and no cooking method to choose.

ideas.title: Preset Snack Cartridge

new_nodes.label: Cartridge reader slot
new_nodes.detail: Inserting a pre-set cartridge loads the cooking program; no panel changes are needed.

ideas.rationale: Users insert the food's cartridge and press nothing, so no settings are ever seen.

ideas.title: Phone-Tap Companion

new_nodes.label: Phone NFC pairing
new_nodes.detail: Tapping a phone to the oven sends the cooking program.

ideas.rationale: Users with a phone can set cooking with a tap they already know how to do.

ideas.title: Stick-On Heat Label

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic reheat sticker
new_nodes.detail: A label on the plate changes colour when the food is hot enough.

ideas.rationale: The plate reports its own state, so users read a colour instead of reading a timer.

ideas.title: Power-Free Lunch Box Warmer

new_nodes.label: Exothermic chemical pad
new_nodes.detail: A chemical pad heats food for twenty minutes once activated.

ideas.rationale: There are no controls at all, only a single pull-tab to start heating.

ideas.title: Bubble-Foil Splatter Cover

new_nodes.label: Disposable splatter film
new_nodes.detail: A microwave-safe film lays over food and is thrown away after use.

ideas.rationale: Users never clean the cavity, which removes a chore that is confusing for beginners.

ideas.title: Self-Cleaning Steam Cavity

new_nodes.label: Steam self-clean cycle
new_nodes.detail: Steam loosens splatter so one wipe is enough.

ideas.rationale: The oven cleans itself so nobody needs a cleaning routine.

ideas.title: Egg-Timer Ring Dial

new_nodes.label: Ring-timer dial
new_nodes.detail: A ring of coloured segments shows time left, with one turn to add time.

ideas.rationale: Colour segments are read instantly and one turn adds time, with no numbers to learn.

ideas.title: Phone Cam Doneness Check

new_nodes.label: Phone camera food read
new_nodes.detail: The phone reads food colour and tells the user when it is ready.

ideas.rationale: Checking through a phone screen avoids opening the oven at all.

ideas.title: Stackable Pod Oven

new_nodes.label: Pod cooking chamber
new_nodes.detail: Each pod is a sealed meal chamber that the oven heats, with no settings.

ideas.rationale: The meal chamber defines the cooking so the oven has nothing for the user to set.

ideas.title: Wall-Mounted Pull Cord

new_nodes.label: Pull-cord starter
new_nodes.detail: A pull cord starts the oven, like a fridge light or a blind.

ideas.rationale: A pull cord is a familiar action with an obvious result, so no reading or learning is needed.

ideas.title: Fold-Down Tray Start

new_nodes.label: Closing-tray trigger
new_nodes.detail: Closing the fold-down tray starts cooking, so the act of loading starts it.

ideas.rationale: Closing the tray is the only step, and it is the same as closing any drawer.

ideas.title: Hourglass Turntable Sand

new_nodes.label: Sand turntable clock
new_nodes.detail: The turntable is a sand disk whose slow sweep shows time elapsed.

ideas.rationale: A visual sweep tells users how long remains without any control or number.

ideas.title: Dead-Man Auto Stop

new_nodes.label: Heat-proof fusible link
new_nodes.detail: A fusible link breaks if the oven overheats and needs no electronics.

ideas.rationale: A simple mechanical fuse protects the user without them ever needing to understand it.

ideas.title: Glowing Ring Status

new_nodes.label: Colour-ring status light
new_nodes.detail: A ring of light changes from red to green to show whether the oven is heating.

ideas.rationale: Red means wait and green means ready, a signal that needs no manual.

ideas.title: Voice Command Only

new_nodes.label: Local voice recognition
new_nodes.detail: The user says 'heat soup' and the oven picks the program.

ideas.rationale: Speaking the food name is simpler than knowing any control or setting.

ideas.title: Glass-Free Bowl Cook

new_nodes.label: Self-rotating cooking bowl
new_nodes.detail: The bowl itself spins on a base when placed in the oven.

ideas.rationale: The bowl is the only object used, so there is no turntable to think about.

ideas.title: Ceramic Mug Heating Puck

new_nodes.label: Mug heating puck
new_nodes.detail: A puck inside a standard mug heats the drink with one press.

ideas.rationale: A mug heater that works with one press needs no oven, timer or door at all.

ideas.title: Phone Projector Cavity

new_nodes.label: Cavity projection
new_nodes.detail: A tiny projector shows the food and cooking status on the glass door.

ideas.rationale: The oven shows what it is doing in plain words on the door, so no manual is needed.

ideas.title: Say-It Cooking

new_nodes.label: Voice microphone
new_nodes.detail: Far-field mic that takes plain requests like 'warm my coffee' and sets time and power automatically.

new_nodes.label: Interpret natural request
new_nodes.detail: Maps everyday speech to cook duration and power level.

ideas.rationale: Speaking a goal removes the need to learn any dial logic at all.

ideas.title: Scan-and-Go Packaging

new_nodes.label: Package reader
new_nodes.detail: Reads a printed code on ready-meal packaging and loads the cook program.

new_nodes.label: Printed cook code
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost machine-readable mark printed on food packaging.

ideas.rationale: The packaging does the setting, so the user only places the food and presses start.

ideas.title: Weigh-and-Heat Plate

new_nodes.label: Load-sensing plate
new_nodes.detail: Turntable underside weighs the food and sets cook time from mass.

new_nodes.label: Auto-set duration
new_nodes.detail: Calculates cook time from the measured load.

ideas.rationale: Weight tells the machine how long to cook, so no time has to be guessed or entered.

ideas.title: Touch-to-Open Door

new_nodes.label: Capacitive door panel
new_nodes.detail: Flat sensor where the door opens when lightly touched, with no button to find.

ideas.rationale: Touching the door works the same way on every microwave, so there is nothing to learn.

ideas.title: Ambient Status Glow

new_nodes.label: Colour-state LED strip
new_nodes.detail: Low-power light around the base that shows cooking as green, amber, or ready.

new_nodes.label: Show cooking state
new_nodes.detail: Communicates progress through colour instead of a number.

ideas.rationale: A colour the user already understands replaces reading labels or timers.

ideas.title: One-Button Cook

new_nodes.label: Single smart button
new_nodes.detail: One large button that starts a sensor-chosen cook for whatever is inside.

ideas.rationale: One button with no settings means nothing needs to be chosen or understood.

ideas.title: Hot-Spot Thermal Cam

new_nodes.label: Infrared sensor
new_nodes.detail: Reads surface temperature and shows cold and hot spots on a simple ring.

new_nodes.label: Detect uneven heating
new_nodes.detail: Sees where food is still cold or overheating.

ideas.rationale: The machine itself reports whether food is ready, so the user doesn't have to judge it.

ideas.title: Hand-Wave Start

new_nodes.label: Gesture sensor
new_nodes.detail: Infrared sensor that starts the cycle when a hand is waved over the door.

ideas.rationale: A wave is a universal gesture that needs no reading or learning.

ideas.title: Close-to-Cook

new_nodes.label: Auto-start on close
new_nodes.detail: Cooking begins as soon as the door latches shut.

ideas.rationale: Closing the door is already a habit, so the start step becomes invisible.

ideas.title: Food-Shaped Tokens

new_nodes.label: Food token tray
new_nodes.detail: Small chunky tokens shaped like pizza, rice, or soup; placing one selects the program.

new_nodes.label: RFID tagging
new_nodes.detail: Passive tags inside tokens that the tray reads.

ideas.rationale: Physical shapes match food types, so choosing a setting is the same as choosing a meal.

ideas.title: Shape-Matched Doorway

new_nodes.label: Picture door panel
new_nodes.detail: Door shows large icons for common foods to tap, with no text.

ideas.rationale: Pictures need no language or instructions and can be read at a glance.

ideas.title: Auto-Power Mode

new_nodes.label: Adaptive duty cycle
new_nodes.detail: Chooses power level from food moisture and mass without user input.

ideas.rationale: Removing the choice of power level removes the most confusing setting.

ideas.title: Haptic Done Pulse

new_nodes.label: Vibration pad
new_nodes.detail: Pad under the front edge that pulses when cooking is complete.

ideas.rationale: A felt pulse signals completion without any sound or reading.

ideas.title: Lift-Up Finish

new_nodes.label: Rising tray
new_nodes.detail: Turntable lifts a few centimetres when cooking is done, so the food rises to meet you.

ideas.rationale: A physical rise is impossible to miss and needs no explanation.

ideas.title: Steam-Stop Sensor

new_nodes.label: Humidity sensor
new_nodes.detail: Stops when steam from the food drops off, signalling the food is done.

ideas.rationale: Steam is visible and intuitive, so the machine stops on what the user already watches for.

ideas.title: Memory Repeat Button

new_nodes.label: Remember last cook
new_nodes.detail: Stores the last successful cook and repeats it on one press.

ideas.rationale: Most users reheat the same things, so the machine learns them and the user never sets anything.

ideas.title: Cook Card Slot

new_nodes.label: Card slot
new_nodes.detail: A slot that accepts a credit-card-sized card; each card is a pre-set meal.

ideas.rationale: Inserting a card is a familiar action that does the setting for the user.

ideas.title: Dinner Dial Plate

new_nodes.label: Single hunger dial
new_nodes.detail: One dial with three marks: snack, meal, feast.

ideas.rationale: Choosing how hungry you are replaces timing and power, which are harder to judge.

ideas.title: Glass Clock Face

new_nodes.label: Clock-face display
new_nodes.detail: A display that looks like a clock; users point the hand to the time they want.

ideas.rationale: Everyone already knows how to read a clock, so the timer needs no explanation.

ideas.title: Always-Gentle Mode

new_nodes.label: Single safe power
new_nodes.detail: Runs every cook at one gentle setting, which is slower but never burns.

ideas.rationale: With one setting there is nothing to choose and nothing to get wrong.

ideas.title: Speaking Microwave

new_nodes.label: Voice prompt speaker
new_nodes.detail: Says the food is ready in plain words, such as 'your soup is done'.

ideas.rationale: A spoken message tells the user what happened, not just that a sound occurred.

ideas.title: Ring-Light Countdown

new_nodes.label: Shrinking LED ring
new_nodes.detail: Ring of lights around the door that goes dark one segment at a time as cooking finishes.

ideas.rationale: A ring that empties is a visual countdown anyone can read at a glance.

ideas.title: Counter Projection

new_nodes.label: Counter projector
new_nodes.detail: Projects the cooking status and buttons onto the counter in front of the machine.

ideas.rationale: Controls appear where the user is already looking, with no panel to study.

ideas.title: Stomp-to-Open

new_nodes.label: Floor pad
new_nodes.detail: A pad on the floor in front of the machine that opens the door when stepped on.

ideas.rationale: Stepping is a reflex that needs no finding or remembering of a button.

ideas.title: Dish Is the Rotor

new_nodes.label: Induction-coupled plate
new_nodes.detail: The serving plate sits on a rotor that spins by induction, so the plate and the spin are one part.

ideas.rationale: Users never separate or wash a turntable, so there is one less thing to handle.

ideas.title: Phased Heating No-Turn

new_nodes.label: Phased heating array
new_nodes.detail: Multiple emitters that heat evenly without any turning.

ideas.rationale: Removing the turntable removes a part that can be put in wrongly or fall off.

ideas.title: Drop-From-Above Tray

new_nodes.label: Top-loading hatch
new_nodes.detail: Food is dropped in through a hatch on the top, which needs no door handling.

ideas.rationale: Dropping food in from above is the simplest motion a person can make.

ideas.title: Sliding Drawer Cooker

new_nodes.label: Drawer chamber
new_nodes.detail: Chamber slides out like a drawer; the food tray stays in place when pulled.

ideas.rationale: A drawer behaves like the kitchen drawers people already know.

ideas.title: Magnet-Latch Door

new_nodes.label: Magnetic seal
new_nodes.detail: A magnetic seal that holds the door closed and releases on a gentle pull.

ideas.rationale: A pull-to-open door needs no button to find or press.

ideas.title: Cook-Anything Puck

new_nodes.label: Smart puck
new_nodes.detail: A flat puck placed on the food; it sends the food type and time to the machine.

ideas.rationale: The food itself carries its own settings, so the user only places it.

ideas.title: Pop-Sound Doneness

new_nodes.label: Acoustic doneness detect
new_nodes.detail: Listens for popping, bubbling, or silence to decide when food is done.

ideas.rationale: The machine judges doneness by sound, so the user doesn't need to time anything.

ideas.title: Recipe Stripe Labels

new_nodes.label: Colour sticker code
new_nodes.detail: A coloured band on packaging that the door reads to choose the cook.

ideas.rationale: Matching colour stripes is easier than reading any settings at all.

ideas.title: Hourglass Window Timer

new_nodes.label: Sand-fill window
new_nodes.detail: A window strip in the door where sand or light fills to show time left.

ideas.rationale: A filling vessel shows elapsed time with no numbers to read.

ideas.title: Mug-Bottom Sensor

new_nodes.label: Container contact pad
new_nodes.detail: A pad under the cup or bowl that reads its material and fill and starts a matching cook.

ideas.rationale: Putting the mug on the pad is a single natural action with no setup.

ideas.title: Pet-Like Reactions

new_nodes.label: Expressive face display
new_nodes.detail: A small face on the door that smiles when food is ready and frowns if the door is open.

ideas.rationale: A face is understood without any manual, so status is clear to anyone.

ideas.title: Kitchen Robot Arm

new_nodes.label: Retrieval arm
new_nodes.detail: A small arm that takes a food tray from the counter, loads it, and returns it when done.

ideas.rationale: The user only places the tray on a pad and the machine handles the rest.

ideas.title: Fridge-Door Interlock

new_nodes.label: Fridge-to-oven sync
new_nodes.detail: Reads the fridge contents and suggests reheating for the item placed in front of it.

ideas.rationale: The machine knows what the food is, so the user doesn't have to tell it.

ideas.title: Paper Cook Card

new_nodes.label: Printed cook card
new_nodes.detail: A paper card with a single printed image and no text; scanning it selects the cook.

ideas.rationale: A printed picture is cheaper than a control panel and needs no learning.

ideas.title: Heat-Reactive Door Glass

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic glass
new_nodes.detail: Glass that changes colour at set temperatures, so the food state shows without light.

ideas.rationale: The door tells you when food is hot, so no bulb or reading is needed.

ideas.title: Preset Breakfast Button

new_nodes.label: Meal-time presets
new_nodes.detail: Chooses a setting based on the time of day, such as breakfast or dinner.

ideas.rationale: The time of day is the setting, so the user doesn't have to choose one.

ideas.title: Wall-Mount Shelf Mode

new_nodes.label: Flat cooking shelf
new_nodes.detail: A shallow shelf that mounts to a wall and heats only the food placed on it.

ideas.rationale: No box or door means there is nothing to open, close, or set up.

ideas.title: Hourly Auto-Reheat

new_nodes.label: Scheduled reheat
new_nodes.detail: Warms food at a fixed time set once, such as meals at 6 pm each day.

ideas.rationale: Once set, the food warms itself and never needs operating again.

ideas.title: Ceramic Bowl Tray

new_nodes.label: Bowl-shaped chamber
new_nodes.detail: Chamber is curved like a bowl, so food always sits in the same centre spot.

ideas.rationale: Food always lands in the same place, so there is nothing to arrange or align.

ideas.title: Fold-Down Front Panel

new_nodes.label: Single flap
new_nodes.detail: Front flap that folds down; the opening reveals a single button when lowered.

ideas.rationale: Hiding the controls until needed leaves a clean surface with almost nothing to read.

ideas.title: Shake-To-Heat

new_nodes.label: Motion sensor cup
new_nodes.detail: A cup with a sensor that starts heating when it is picked up and shaken.

ideas.rationale: Shaking to start is a natural action that needs no buttons or instructions.

ideas.title: Tap-to-Warm Lid

new_nodes.label: Lid tap pad
new_nodes.detail: A pad on the lid that starts or stops heating when tapped once.

ideas.rationale: A tap on the lid is the simplest interaction a machine can offer.

ideas.title: Sun-Warm Ring

new_nodes.label: Passive warming ring
new_nodes.detail: A ring that warms food slowly on a counter once placed, with no settings.

ideas.rationale: Placing a plate on the ring is the entire operation.

ideas.title: Bell-Free Silence

new_nodes.label: Mute-by-default signal
new_nodes.detail: Signals completion through a glowing ring with no sound unless requested.

ideas.rationale: Silent, visual completion removes any need to know what the sound means.

ideas.title: Dial-Less Wheel

new_nodes.label: Scroll wheel
new_nodes.detail: One wheel that scrolls through the foods and stops at the one that matches.

ideas.rationale: Scrolling a list of food names is simpler than choosing a time and power pair.

ideas.title: Air-Crisp Fan Mode

new_nodes.label: Crisp by air
new_nodes.detail: A fan that crisps food so that a microwave is never used on the wrong food.

ideas.rationale: One mode covers the common mistake of wrong results, so the user does not need to pick the right mode.

ideas.title: Wearable Cook Cue

new_nodes.label: Watch notification
new_nodes.detail: Sends a vibration to a watch when the food is ready, so the kitchen doesn't need to be watched.

ideas.rationale: Users are notified wherever they are, so no reading or attention is needed at the machine.

ideas.title: Snap-On Food Caps

new_nodes.label: Snap-on cap
new_nodes.detail: A cap on the food container that clicks into place and sets time and power through its shape.

ideas.rationale: A cap that only fits one way cannot be set wrong, so no learning is needed.

ideas.title: Always-Ready Standby

new_nodes.label: Instant reheat on touch
new_nodes.detail: Stays warm in standby so any food placed in it heats without any setting.

ideas.rationale: Constant readiness means the user never has to start or set anything.

ideas.title: Just Heat It: one-button auto-cook

new_nodes.label: Single start button with food-sensing core
new_nodes.detail: One large button; an IR/humidity sensor array estimates food mass and sets time and power automatically.

new_nodes.label: Starts sensible cook with one press
new_nodes.detail: Removes all manual choice from the user.
