ideas.rationale: A sheet that is thrown away after use is simpler than wiping mica that is hard to reach.

ideas.title: Chopstick Thermometer Probe

new_nodes.label: Disposable food probe
new_nodes.detail: Probe inserted into food sends a temperature reading to the controller

ideas.rationale: The probe tells the appliance when the food is safe, so the user never has to guess.

ideas.title: Anti-Superheat Ring

new_nodes.label: Liquid-cup nucleation stick
new_nodes.detail: Dipped stick provides nucleation points so liquids boil gently without eruption

ideas.rationale: Liquids heat safely with no special wait or technique, so drinks are ready without fear of boiling over.

ideas.title: Hot-Drink Shot Button

new_nodes.label: Preset drink heating
new_nodes.detail: One press heats any cup of liquid to a safe drinking temperature

ideas.rationale: Breakfast drinks are ready with one press, which is the simplest possible way to deliver the result.

ideas.title: Freeze-Aware Auto Defrost

new_nodes.label: Weight-based auto defrost
new_nodes.detail: Load cell reads frozen mass and runs a defrost program with no setting

ideas.rationale: The user puts frozen food in and presses one button, so defrosting needs no knowledge of times or power levels.

ideas.title: Tap-to-Melt Butter Tray

new_nodes.label: Single-press soften mode
new_nodes.detail: Pressing the butter icon softens butter for cake baking with no setting

ideas.rationale: A dedicated icon for softening butter removes the guesswork that baking tasks normally need.

ideas.title: Recipe Card Scanner

new_nodes.label: Phone-camera recipe capture
new_nodes.detail: Phone camera reads a printed recipe card and sends settings to the oven

ideas.rationale: Users point their phone at a recipe and the machine does the rest, so no settings need to be read or typed.

ideas.title: Hands-Free Voice Cook

new_nodes.label: Wake-word speech recognition
new_nodes.detail: Speaking heat for two minutes starts a cooking program with simple phrases

ideas.rationale: Speaking a plain request is more natural than any knob, and it lets people walk away while cooking.

ideas.title: Stand-Still Remote Phone Ping

new_nodes.label: Phone notification on done
new_nodes.detail: Oven sends a push notification to a paired phone when cooking ends

ideas.rationale: The user learns that food is ready from their phone, so they never have to stand and wait beside the oven.

ideas.title: Radiation-Safe Mesh Replacement

new_nodes.label: Transparent conductive oxide door film
new_nodes.detail: Thin ITO film on glass blocks microwaves while showing the cavity clearly

ideas.rationale: A clear full-view door lets the user see the food without any mesh to clean or get hot.

ideas.title: Look-Through Sealed Door Glass

new_nodes.label: Solid glass door panel
new_nodes.detail: Full-size tempered glass panel with conductive coating and no holes

ideas.rationale: A clean, unbroken window is easy to read and easy to wipe down.

ideas.title: Tall Tower Cavity

new_nodes.label: Vertical stacked cavity
new_nodes.detail: Tall narrow cavity with a rotating tray stack for small footprints

ideas.rationale: A narrow tower fits on a small counter and is simple to understand from the front.

ideas.title: Dual-Plug Universal Converter

new_nodes.label: Auto-ranging mains input
new_nodes.detail: Input stage accepts 100 to 240 V and adjusts drive automatically

ideas.rationale: One model works anywhere, so users never have to check or set the voltage.

ideas.title: Shared-Kitchen Lock Mode

new_nodes.label: Tap-card access
new_nodes.detail: Office card opens the door and starts the oven for an authorized user

ideas.rationale: Only the right people can use it, and each person opens it with the card they already carry.

ideas.title: Child-Proof by Design

new_nodes.label: Safe-by-default start
new_nodes.detail: Oven only starts when the door is closed and a fixed tap pattern is used

ideas.rationale: The machine simply does not start in unsafe conditions, so the family never has to remember rules.

ideas.title: Recycled-Parts Modular Knobs

new_nodes.label: Snap-on modular control module
new_nodes.detail: Control module clips on as one part and can be swapped without tools

ideas.rationale: Parts snap in with no screws, so the cheapest build is also the easiest to assemble and service.

ideas.title: Fused Fascia Single Molding

new_nodes.label: Single-shot injection-molded fascia
new_nodes.detail: One molded part forms the whole control panel with embossed controls

ideas.rationale: A simple, sealed panel has no gaps to clean and no extra parts for the user to worry about.

ideas.title: Cord-Free Carry Handle Oven

new_nodes.label: Built-in handle with cord storage
new_nodes.detail: Top handle wraps and stores the cord inside its body

ideas.rationale: The cord is always neatly stored, so there is nothing to tangle or untangle before cooking.

ideas.title: Silent Mode as Default

new_nodes.label: Quiet overnight mode
new_nodes.detail: Oven ignores the bell and fan at night and uses silent alerts

ideas.rationale: Quiet behaviour happens without any setting, so the appliance fits into family life without a menu to learn.

ideas.title: Glowing Feel-Good Light

new_nodes.label: Mood-cook lighting
new_nodes.detail: Cavity lighting shifts to warm tones that make reheating feel comforting

ideas.rationale: A warm, inviting light turns a simple reheat into a pleasant moment, with no controls to learn.

ideas.title: Food Picture Drum

new_nodes.label: Rotating picture drum
new_nodes.detail: A single dial showing pictures of rice, soup, popcorn and leftovers; each picture sets time and power together.

new_nodes.label: Selects food preset
new_nodes.detail: Chooses duration and power in one turn by recognising the food shown.

ideas.rationale: Replacing two numeric dials with one picture drum removes the need to know times or power levels, so anyone can cook without instruction.

ideas.title: Heat-Until-Done Button

new_nodes.label: Steam-humidity sensing
new_nodes.detail: A humidity sensor in the vent detects when food releases steam and stops heating automatically.

ideas.rationale: One button that starts cooking and stops it when food is ready means the user never needs to guess a time.

ideas.title: Visible Sand-Timer Window

new_nodes.label: Sand-fill timer strip
new_nodes.detail: A clear strip on the door where a coloured band drains from top to bottom as cooking proceeds.

ideas.rationale: A draining band is understood at a glance and needs no reading of digits, which serves users unfamiliar with timers.

ideas.title: Three Emoji Buttons

new_nodes.label: Three pictogram buttons
new_nodes.detail: Large buttons marked with a flame, a pot and a snowflake for cook, simmer and defrost.

ideas.rationale: Three symbols replace a five-step numeric knob, so the power choice is obvious without any manual.

ideas.title: Weigh-to-Power Mat

new_nodes.label: Load-cell cooking mat
new_nodes.detail: A flat plate under the turntable that weighs the food and sets time and power from its mass.

ideas.rationale: Placing food on the mat is the only action needed, because the machine works out the rest from weight.

ideas.title: Hip-Bump Auto Door

new_nodes.label: Proximity door opener
new_nodes.detail: A sensor on the handle side opens the door when a hand or hip approaches with a full load.

ideas.rationale: Opening the door by approaching it requires no known gesture, which helps someone whose hands are full.

ideas.title: Palm Panel Release

new_nodes.label: Full-width soft panel
new_nodes.detail: A broad, cushioned strip along the bottom of the door that opens it when pressed by any part of the hand.

ideas.rationale: A large target that accepts any press means the user cannot miss it, so there is no need to find a small button.

ideas.title: Tap-Glass to Open

new_nodes.label: Vibration tap detection
new_nodes.detail: An accelerometer in the door detects two taps on the glass and releases the latch.

ideas.rationale: Tapping the glass is an instinctive gesture that needs no searching for a button.

ideas.title: Magnetic Self-Latch Door

new_nodes.label: Magnetic self-latching catch
new_nodes.detail: A magnet closes and holds the door when it is pushed shut, and releases when pulled firmly.

ideas.rationale: The door latches itself on closing, so the user never has to think about the latch.

ideas.title: Sliding Pocket Door

new_nodes.label: Sliding glass pocket door
new_nodes.detail: A door that slides sideways into the side of the cabinet instead of swinging on hinges.

ideas.rationale: A door that slides needs no swing clearance and cannot swing into a person, which is easy to use in any kitchen.

ideas.title: Float-Hinge Door

new_nodes.label: Friction-free float hinge
new_nodes.detail: A hinge that holds the door at any angle with a gentle, constant resistance.

ideas.rationale: A door that stays where it is left needs no prop or effort, which is simple for anyone to use.

ideas.title: Lift-Lid Top Opening

new_nodes.label: Top-lift lid
new_nodes.detail: The cavity opens by lifting the top like a slow cooker lid, with the window on the top.

ideas.rationale: Lifting a lid is a motion everyone already knows, so the door needs no explanation.

ideas.title: Fully Transparent Cabinet

new_nodes.label: Transparent conductive glass
new_nodes.detail: A coated glass shell that reflects microwaves but passes visible light across the whole front.

ideas.rationale: A front that is see-through everywhere means the user can check food without looking for a window.

ideas.title: Projected Cooking View

new_nodes.label: Interior camera with projector
new_nodes.detail: A small camera inside sends a live image to a screen on the outside of the door.

ideas.rationale: A large live image on the door shows food state clearly, even for users with poor eyesight.

ideas.title: Glowing Phosphor Cavity

new_nodes.label: Charged phosphor coating
new_nodes.detail: A coating inside the cavity that glows softly after a brief charge from the door LED strip.

ideas.rationale: The cavity stays visible without a bulb that has to be replaced or switched on.

ideas.title: Door-Open Light Ring

new_nodes.label: Edge light ring
new_nodes.detail: A thin LED ring around the door frame that lights only when the door opens.

ideas.rationale: Light appears exactly when the door opens, so no switch is needed.

ideas.title: Aroma Done Signal

new_nodes.label: Scent release module
new_nodes.detail: A small capsule releases a pleasant smell when cooking ends, which is noticed by people who cannot hear a bell.

ideas.rationale: A scent signal reaches people with hearing loss and needs no understanding of a sound code.

ideas.title: Tilting Plate Finish

new_nodes.label: Tilting turntable
new_nodes.detail: At the end of cooking, the glass plate tilts gently toward the user to show that cooking is over.

ideas.rationale: A visible movement at the end of cooking is clear without any sound or reading.

ideas.title: Pull-Cord Timer

new_nodes.label: Retractable pull cord
new_nodes.detail: The user pulls a cord to the length they want, and it slowly retracts while cooking runs.

ideas.rationale: A longer pull means more time, which is understood directly by physical length.

ideas.title: Wind-Up Spring Timer

new_nodes.label: Mechanical wind-up spring
new_nodes.detail: A crank winds a spring that unwinds slowly, with the visible coil showing the remaining time.

ideas.rationale: A crank that unwinds needs no electronics, and the coil shows how much time is left.

ideas.title: Sliding Block Counter

new_nodes.label: Stackable time blocks
new_nodes.detail: Each block is one minute; the user places blocks on a tray and they drop off as time passes.

ideas.rationale: Counting physical blocks is concrete and needs no reading of numbers.

ideas.title: Packaging Reads Settings

new_nodes.label: Packet code reader
new_nodes.detail: The microwave reads a code printed on ready-meal packs and sets time and power automatically.

ideas.rationale: The food packaging carries the settings, so the user only places the pack and presses start.

ideas.title: Tap-to-Cook Tray

new_nodes.label: NFC cooking tray
new_nodes.detail: A tray with a chip that tells the microwave the food's settings when placed inside.

ideas.rationale: Placing the tray is the only action, so no settings need to be chosen.

ideas.title: Single Start Pad

new_nodes.label: One large start pad
new_nodes.detail: A single pad that starts a cycle chosen automatically from what the camera sees on the turntable.

ideas.rationale: One pad is the entire interface, so there is nothing to learn.

ideas.title: Camera Auto-Program

new_nodes.label: Food recognition camera
new_nodes.detail: A camera identifies the food and sets power and time without user input.

ideas.rationale: The machine chooses settings by seeing the food, so the user has nothing to decide.

ideas.title: Habit-Learning Preset

new_nodes.label: Usage pattern learner
new_nodes.detail: The machine remembers what is cooked most often and presets it when the door opens.

ideas.rationale: The most common setting is already chosen, so regular use takes no thought.

ideas.title: Continuous Smooth Power

new_nodes.label: Inverter magnetron supply
new_nodes.detail: A solid-state supply that runs the magnetron at any continuous power without cycling.

ideas.rationale: Smooth power removes the on-off pulsing that confuses users, so food heats evenly.

ideas.title: Heat Gauge Slider

new_nodes.label: Thermometer slider
new_nodes.detail: A vertical slider with a red-to-blue gauge that fills up to show the heat level.

ideas.rationale: A gauge filling up is read as intensity with no numbers.

ideas.title: Glow-Ring Countdown

new_nodes.label: Shrinking light ring
new_nodes.detail: A glowing ring around the plate that shrinks as cooking goes on and vanishes at the end.

ideas.rationale: A ring that visibly shrinks shows progress from across the room.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Plate Ring

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic indicator band
new_nodes.detail: A band around the plate changes colour as the cooking zone heats and cools.

ideas.rationale: A colour change shows whether food is still cooking, which needs no understanding of time.

ideas.title: Automatic Universal Voltage

new_nodes.label: Universal input supply
new_nodes.detail: A supply that accepts any mains voltage and frequency without a switch.

ideas.rationale: No voltage setting means no choice for the user to get wrong when moving the machine.

ideas.title: Stationary Cavity Mode Stirrer

new_nodes.label: Mode stirrer fan
new_nodes.detail: A rotating metal vane spreads microwaves so the turntable is not needed.

ideas.rationale: Removing the glass plate means nothing can be misplaced or lifted off its track.

ideas.title: Dome Cloche Cooker

new_nodes.label: Dome lid
new_nodes.detail: A microwave dome that lowers over a plate and needs no door, just a lift.

ideas.rationale: A dome placed over a plate is as simple as putting a cover on a dish.

ideas.title: Drawer Microwave

new_nodes.label: Pull-out cooking drawer
new_nodes.detail: The cavity is a drawer that slides out toward the user with the food on a flat tray.

ideas.rationale: Pulling a drawer out brings the food to the user without reaching into a hot cavity.

ideas.title: Floor-Level Ramp Door

new_nodes.label: Low-slung ramp door
new_nodes.detail: The cavity sits at waist height and opens by a ramp that lowers the food toward the user.

ideas.rationale: Placing the cavity at a comfortable height removes the need to bend or lift for older users.

ideas.title: Molded Shell Housing

new_nodes.label: Conductive polymer molding
new_nodes.detail: A single moulded shell with a conductive coating replaces the stamped steel wrapper and hinges.

ideas.rationale: A single moulded part is cheaper to make and avoids parts that could catch the user's fingers.

ideas.title: Die-Cast One-Piece Cavity

new_nodes.label: Single die-cast tub
new_nodes.detail: The cavity is one die-cast aluminium piece with no spot welds.

ideas.rationale: Fewer parts mean fewer seams and less risk of a loose part for the user to handle.

ideas.title: Bounce-Back Tab Door

new_nodes.label: Spring tab release
new_nodes.detail: A tab at the door edge that springs the door open a few centimetres when pressed.

ideas.rationale: A door that opens a little on its own is a clear cue that it has released.

ideas.title: Knock-to-Open Door

new_nodes.label: Acoustic knock sensor
new_nodes.detail: A microphone detects a knock on the door and releases the latch.

ideas.rationale: A knock is a natural gesture that needs no button location.

ideas.title: Wearable Presence Stop

new_nodes.label: Wrist beacon
new_nodes.detail: A wristband that tells the oven when the wearer returns to the kitchen, pausing heating.

ideas.rationale: Pausing when the user is near means the user does not have to remember to stop it.

ideas.title: Hanging Hook Timer

new_nodes.label: Pegboard timer pins
new_nodes.detail: The user pushes a pin into a row of holes; the pin count sets the minutes.

ideas.rationale: Pushing a pin into a visible hole is a direct and tactile act that needs no reading.

ideas.title: Glass Tap-to-Stop Interface

new_nodes.label: Tap-to-stop window
new_nodes.detail: Tapping the window stops the microwave and opens the door in one gesture.

ideas.rationale: One tap on the window handles stopping and opening, which is very easy to remember.

ideas.title: Cord-Free Sensor Plate

new_nodes.label: Flat sensor plate
new_nodes.detail: A low, flat pad on the counter that replaces the entire control panel.

ideas.rationale: A flat surface with no buttons or knobs is easy to clean and to learn.

ideas.title: Voice-Free Gesture Air Control

new_nodes.label: Hand-wave sensor
new_nodes.detail: A sensor above the door reads an upward wave for more heat and a downward wave for less.

ideas.rationale: Simple hand movements are natural and need no buttons to be found.

ideas.title: Ambient Smell Preheat

new_nodes.label: Smell-based heat matching
new_nodes.detail: The microwave reads food smell to pick the right heat level automatically.

ideas.rationale: Choosing power by sensing the food removes the need to make any setting.

ideas.title: Shared Cooking Sync

new_nodes.label: Caregiver sync alert
new_nodes.detail: The microwave sends a message to a family member's phone when cooking ends.

ideas.rationale: A relative who knows the food is ready means the elderly user does not need to track timing alone.

ideas.title: Two-Tone Done Pattern

new_nodes.label: Vibrating base alert
new_nodes.detail: The microwave vibrates the counter gently at the end of cooking instead of ringing a bell.

ideas.rationale: A felt vibration is noticed by people who cannot hear the bell.

ideas.title: Sealed Container Cooking

new_nodes.label: Sealed cooking jar
new_nodes.detail: A sealed jar with a built-in heat setting that the microwave reads from its base.

ideas.rationale: The container handles power and time, so the microwave needs no user input.

ideas.title: Cook-Time Strip Calendar

new_nodes.label: Pictogram time strip
new_nodes.detail: A strip with pictures of food and a time line; the user slides a marker to the picture.

ideas.rationale: Sliding a marker to a picture is intuitive and needs no understanding of units.

ideas.title: Plug-and-Heat Stand

new_nodes.label: Detachable heat stand
new_nodes.detail: A low-cost stand that holds the cavity and plugs in with no separate controls.

ideas.rationale: A stand with one plug and no controls cuts cost while staying simple to use.

ideas.title: Snap-and-Cook Camera

new_nodes.label: Food-recognition camera
new_nodes.detail: Small camera in the roof identifies the food and sets time and power automatically.

ideas.rationale: The user places food inside and presses one button, so no settings need to be learned.

ideas.title: Plate NFC Auto-Cook

new_nodes.label: NFC tag on food packaging
new_nodes.detail: Ready-meal packs carry a tag that tells the oven the exact cook profile.

ideas.rationale: Tapping the pack to the oven replaces all manual settings, so there is nothing to figure out.

ideas.title: Weigh-and-Go Tray

new_nodes.label: Load-cell turntable sensor
new_nodes.detail: The turntable measures mass and sets cook time from the weight alone.

ideas.rationale: Mass is the only input needed, so the user never estimates minutes.

ideas.title: Single Pictogram Dial

new_nodes.label: Four-icon food dial
new_nodes.detail: One dial with icons for drink, leftovers, frozen meal, and popcorn.

ideas.rationale: Choosing a picture is more intuitive than reading numbers or power levels.

ideas.title: Three-Word Mood Power

new_nodes.label: Soft, Normal, Done selection
new_nodes.detail: The five power steps collapse into three plain-language choices.

ideas.rationale: Three words are easier to remember than five numbered steps.

ideas.title: Spoken Status Oven

new_nodes.label: Voice speaker
new_nodes.detail: Speaks plain sentences such as Your soup is hot and Stop, it is ready.

ideas.rationale: Clear spoken status removes the need to interpret a bell or a timer.

ideas.title: Scent Done Signal

new_nodes.label: Aroma emitter
new_nodes.detail: Releases a mild popcorn or bread scent when cooking finishes.

ideas.rationale: A smell is an instinctive signal that needs no reading or learning.

ideas.title: Lean-to-Open Door

new_nodes.label: Pressure-sensing door panel
new_nodes.detail: Pushing the door anywhere opens it, with no button to find.

ideas.rationale: Leaning on the door is a natural motion, so there is no button to locate.

ideas.title: Drawer Microwave

new_nodes.label: Pull-out cooking drawer
new_nodes.detail: The cavity slides out like a drawer, showing the food on a flat tray.

ideas.rationale: A drawer matches how people already open kitchen storage, so it needs no learning.

ideas.title: Gravity Latch Door

new_nodes.label: Gravity-weighted latch
new_nodes.detail: The door stays closed by weight alone and opens with a gentle pull.

ideas.rationale: No latch to release means nothing to figure out or press.

ideas.title: Knock-to-Open Door

new_nodes.label: Acoustic knock sensor
new_nodes.detail: A single knock on the door face releases the latch.

ideas.rationale: Knocking on a door is a universal gesture that anyone understands.

ideas.title: Stop-When-Opened Timer

new_nodes.label: Pause on door open
new_nodes.detail: Opening the door pauses cooking, and closing it resumes.

ideas.rationale: Users can check food without worrying about the timer or safety.

ideas.title: Steam-Stop Glass

new_nodes.label: Condensation sensor on door glass
new_nodes.detail: Stops cooking when steam condenses on the door window.

ideas.rationale: Steam is a visible sign of done, so the oven needs no time to set.

ideas.title: Hourglass Timer

new_nodes.label: Visible hourglass chamber
new_nodes.detail: A transparent chamber of fine grains empties at the rate of the cook cycle.

ideas.rationale: Watching sand fall shows remaining time at a glance without reading a dial.

ideas.title: Ambient Glow Done Light

new_nodes.label: Edge-lit casing LED
new_nodes.detail: The outer casing glows a soft color that changes as food finishes.

ideas.rationale: Color conveys status without anyone needing to read or interpret text.

ideas.title: Phosphor Glow Interior

new_nodes.label: Phosphorescent cavity coating
new_nodes.detail: The interior glows faintly after power is applied and stays visible without a bulb.

ideas.rationale: No bulb to replace or switch means the cavity is always visible with zero controls.

ideas.title: Fully Transparent Shell

new_nodes.label: Clear heat-resistant shell
new_nodes.detail: The whole oven is transparent so the food is visible from any angle.

ideas.rationale: Full visibility removes the need to open the door just to check food.

ideas.title: Stirring Antenna Instead of Turntable

new_nodes.label: Mode stirrer
new_nodes.detail: A rotating metal vane spreads microwaves evenly without any tray to place.

ideas.rationale: With no turntable to fit, users place food anywhere and it heats evenly.

ideas.title: Turntable-Free Flat Floor

new_nodes.label: Flat ceramic cavity floor
new_nodes.detail: A stationary floor with no tray, easy to wipe clean.

ideas.rationale: Removing a loose part eliminates a common source of confusion and cleaning.

ideas.title: Self-Wiping Cavity

new_nodes.label: Catalytic cavity coating
new_nodes.detail: A coating that breaks down food splatter during heating, so the cavity stays clean.

ideas.rationale: Users never have to clean or learn a cleaning cycle.

ideas.title: Tap-to-Start Cup Coaster

new_nodes.label: Infrared cup coaster
new_nodes.detail: Placing a cup on the coaster heats it until the target temperature is reached.

ideas.rationale: A single drop-and-go coaster asks no decisions from the user.

ideas.title: Fill-Line Mug Cook

new_nodes.label: Fill-line mug sensor
new_nodes.detail: Placing a mug with a fill line sets the cook time based on the liquid level.

ideas.rationale: Pouring to a mark is a skill everyone already has, so no time guessing is needed.

ideas.title: Always-Two-Minutes Cycle

new_nodes.label: Single adaptive cycle
new_nodes.detail: One press runs a cycle that senses the food and stops itself.

ideas.rationale: A single button with one outcome has the lowest possible learning curve.

ideas.title: One-Button Oven

new_nodes.label: Single start button
new_nodes.detail: The only control, which starts the adaptive cycle.

ideas.rationale: With only one control, there is no panel to read or understand.

ideas.title: Voice-Only Cooking

new_nodes.label: Natural-language microphone
new_nodes.detail: The user says what they want to heat and the oven confirms.

ideas.rationale: Speaking a request is the simplest interface for anyone.

ideas.title: Sliding Heat Ribbon

new_nodes.label: Continuous heat slider
new_nodes.detail: A slider from cold to hot with no numbered steps, showing a color gradient.

ideas.rationale: A slider from cold to hot needs no numbers and maps naturally to intensity.

ideas.title: Dial-Free Touch Surface

new_nodes.label: Single-option touch panel
new_nodes.detail: Only one choice is shown at a time, with a large Next arrow.

ideas.rationale: Showing one choice at a time removes overload for new users.

ideas.title: Haptic Done Pulse

new_nodes.label: Door-handle vibrator
new_nodes.detail: The door handle gently vibrates when cooking finishes.

ideas.rationale: The handle tells you when it is done, even from another room of the kitchen.

ideas.title: Wearable Done Ring

new_nodes.label: Paired wearable buzzer
new_nodes.detail: A ring or bracelet buzzes when the food is ready.

ideas.rationale: A personal alert reaches the user anywhere in the house without setup.

ideas.title: Ceiling Projection Timer

new_nodes.label: Countertop projector
new_nodes.detail: Projects a huge countdown and a done symbol onto the counter.

ideas.rationale: A large projected countdown is readable from across the room.

ideas.title: Magnetic Food Shelf

new_nodes.label: Magnetic levitating tray
new_nodes.detail: A tray floats above the floor, rotating silently with no mechanism.

ideas.rationale: Nothing mechanical to get stuck, so the tray never needs fixing.

ideas.title: Swing-Out Pizza Door

new_nodes.label: Bottom-hinged door
new_nodes.detail: The door drops down to form a shelf, holding food at the right height.

ideas.rationale: A door that doubles as a shelf is intuitive and removes a second step.

ideas.title: Silicone Curtain Door

new_nodes.label: Flexible silicone curtain
new_nodes.detail: A soft heat-safe curtain that pushes open and springs shut.

ideas.rationale: A curtain you push through needs no handle, latch, or button.

ideas.title: Food-Weight Memory Plate

new_nodes.label: Labelled food pads
new_nodes.detail: Plates with printed food icons pair with the oven to set default cycles.

ideas.rationale: Icons on a plate replace settings, so the user just matches picture to food.

ideas.title: Pre-Cooked Pod Oven

new_nodes.label: Sealed meal pod reader
new_nodes.detail: The oven runs the full cycle for a sealed pod, using the code printed on it.

ideas.rationale: Putting in a pod and pressing start is the only action required.

ideas.title: Hob-Microwave Hybrid Pad

new_nodes.label: Heat pad surface
new_nodes.detail: A flat warm surface that heats a dish the way a hot plate does.

ideas.rationale: Plates heat as they would on a stove, which is familiar and simple.

ideas.title: Kettle-Style Lid Oven

new_nodes.label: Top-lift lid
new_nodes.detail: The whole top lifts off like a kettle lid to load the food.

ideas.rationale: Lifting a lid is an instinct that needs no instruction.

ideas.title: Touch-Plate Starter

new_nodes.label: Food-contact start plate
new_nodes.detail: Touching the food to a plate on the oven starts cooking.

ideas.rationale: Starting by touching the food is direct, so there is nothing to find.

ideas.title: Colour-Coded Tray Cook

new_nodes.label: Colour-ring tray
new_nodes.detail: Each tray colour maps to a fixed cook program.

ideas.rationale: Matching colours is easier than reading settings, and children can do it too.

ideas.title: Sound-Cooked Oven

new_nodes.label: Acoustic doneness sensor
new_nodes.detail: Listens to food sounds such as popping or bubbling to decide when to stop.

ideas.rationale: The oven decides when food is done, so the user never needs to check it.

ideas.title: Two-Zone Ultra-Simple

new_nodes.label: Hot and cold zones
new_nodes.detail: A split interior with a single hot zone that is the only choice.

new_nodes.label: One choice only
new_nodes.detail: The machine offers only hot or not hot.

ideas.rationale: Offering only one choice removes the need to decide or learn anything.

ideas.title: Weighted Lid Latch

new_nodes.label: Gravity latch
new_nodes.detail: A door that closes and locks by its own weight, with no catch.

new_nodes.label: Lock by gravity
new_nodes.detail: The door locks itself when closed.

ideas.rationale: Closing the door is the only action, and locking happens automatically.

ideas.title: Flat Kitchen Drawer

new_nodes.label: Pull-out drawer
new_nodes.detail: The cooking chamber is a drawer that slides out to load food.

new_nodes.label: Load by sliding
new_nodes.detail: Food is loaded by sliding the drawer, as with a dishwasher.

ideas.rationale: Sliding a drawer is a motion everyone already knows from kitchen appliances.

ideas.title: Probe-Start Cook

new_nodes.label: Insertion probe
new_nodes.detail: A probe inserted into the food starts and stops cooking by its own reading.

new_nodes.label: Cook by probe
new_nodes.detail: The probe decides when to heat and when to stop.

ideas.rationale: Pushing a probe in is a clear physical action that sets everything up.

ideas.title: Ambient Room Power

new_nodes.label: Room-sensing power unit
new_nodes.detail: Sets power using the room temperature and the food temperature together.

new_nodes.label: Auto-tune power
new_nodes.detail: Power is chosen automatically from the conditions present.

ideas.rationale: The user never sets a power level because the machine chooses the right one.

ideas.title: Frosted Glass Preset Panel

new_nodes.label: Touch-glass panel
new_nodes.detail: A flat glass surface where the only active area lights up when needed.

new_nodes.label: Show controls only when needed
new_nodes.detail: The panel is blank until the user needs it.

ideas.rationale: Hiding controls until needed reduces visible complexity to zero.

ideas.title: Pet-Proof Food Cooker

new_nodes.label: Presence-safe door
new_nodes.detail: The door stays shut while any movement is detected inside.

new_nodes.label: Auto-safe operation
new_nodes.detail: Safety is handled by the machine so no rules need learning.

ideas.rationale: Safety is automatic, so the user never has to remember safety rules.

ideas.title: Hot-Food Fidget Dial

new_nodes.label: Spin-to-pick dial
new_nodes.detail: A dial that spins freely and clicks through the dishes as it is turned.

new_nodes.label: Pick dish by spinning
new_nodes.detail: A spin selects the dish, which is then confirmed by pressing.

ideas.rationale: Spinning is a playful motion that is easy to repeat until the right dish appears.

ideas.title: Print-On-Plate Settings

new_nodes.label: Heat-printing plate
new_nodes.detail: A plate that prints the cooking instruction onto its surface after each use.

new_nodes.label: Remember by printing
new_nodes.detail: The plate remembers last settings by showing them.

ideas.rationale: Settings are remembered on the plate so the user never has to recall them.

ideas.title: Doorstop Power Gauge

new_nodes.label: Analogue heat gauge
new_nodes.detail: A needle gauge on the door that rises with the heat level.

new_nodes.label: Read heat as a needle
new_nodes.detail: The user reads the heat as a needle position on a gauge.

ideas.rationale: A needle gauge shows status at a glance and is easy to read without training.

ideas.title: Auto-Dim Screenless Clock

new_nodes.label: Shadow sundial
new_nodes.detail: A small shadow on the top of the machine that moves with the cooking cycle.

new_nodes.label: Show time by shadow
new_nodes.detail: The cook state is shown by a moving shadow.

ideas.rationale: A shadow needs no electronics and is understood instantly.

ideas.title: Chime-Free Clapper

new_nodes.label: Clap-start sensor
new_nodes.detail: Starts cooking with a clap and stops with a second clap.

new_nodes.label: Start and stop by clap
new_nodes.detail: A clap controls the machine.

ideas.rationale: Clapping is a universal action that works without finding or reading any control.

ideas.title: Eat-Now Pizza Stone

new_nodes.label: Single-food preset plate
new_nodes.detail: A plate that is pre-set for one food type by its surface pattern.

new_nodes.label: Choose food by plate
new_nodes.detail: The food type is set by which plate is used.

ideas.rationale: Choosing a plate needs no setting, since the plate already knows the food.

ideas.title: Bell-Free Cloud Alert

new_nodes.label: Cloud ping relay
new_nodes.detail: Sends a message to the user's phone when food is ready, using their existing app.

new_nodes.label: Alert through existing phone
new_nodes.detail: The user hears of completion on a device they already use.

ideas.rationale: Using a device the user already knows means nothing new to learn.

ideas.title: Mirror-Surface Oven Wall

new_nodes.label: Reflective cavity
new_nodes.detail: A mirrored cavity that shows the food from all sides through reflection.

new_nodes.label: See all sides by reflection
new_nodes.detail: Food is seen from several angles with no moving parts.

ideas.rationale: Reflections give full visibility without any moving part to maintain.

ideas.title: Ice-Cube Start Tray

new_nodes.label: Cube-count starter
new_nodes.detail: Starts a program based on the number of cubes or pieces in the tray.

new_nodes.label: Start by counting
new_nodes.detail: The number of pieces sets the cook time.

ideas.rationale: Counting pieces is a simple physical act that determines cooking time.

ideas.title: Snap-Fit Icon Keys

new_nodes.label: Three-icon key set
new_nodes.detail: Three physical keys with icons for reheat, cook and defrost.

new_nodes.label: Use icon keys
new_nodes.detail: The user presses the icon matching the job.

ideas.rationale: Three icons remove any need to understand power levels or settings.

ideas.title: Glass-Only Touch Surface

new_nodes.label: Feather-touch glass
new_nodes.detail: The glass top responds to a light touch in any place, with no printed buttons.

new_nodes.label: Touch anywhere to start
new_nodes.detail: Any touch on the glass starts cooking.

ideas.rationale: No button has to be located, because any touch is accepted.

ideas.title: Cord-Pull Start

new_nodes.label: Pull-cord starter
new_nodes.detail: A cord that is pulled once to start a cook and pulled again to stop.

new_nodes.label: Start by pull cord
new_nodes.detail: A single pull controls the whole cook.

ideas.rationale: A pull cord is a familiar mechanism, like a lawnmower starter, that requires no reading.

ideas.title: Ember Warm-Keep Plate

new_nodes.label: Auto-hold warmer
new_nodes.detail: Keeps food warm after cooking ends so the user can return later with no reset.

new_nodes.label: Hold warmth automatically
new_nodes.detail: Food stays warm until removed.

ideas.rationale: Food stays warm without any action, so there is no need to restart or time it.

ideas.title: Smart Lid Gravity Timer

new_nodes.label: Timed weight lid
new_nodes.detail: A lid whose weight slowly lowers to indicate how long is left.

new_nodes.label: Show time by lid height
new_nodes.detail: The lid height shows remaining time.

ideas.rationale: A lid that visibly lowers shows time physically without any reading.

ideas.title: Hand-Shaped Heat Control

new_nodes.label: Palm-press heat plate
new_nodes.detail: The user presses a palm onto the plate, and the heat rises with pressure.

new_nodes.label: Set heat by pressure
new_nodes.detail: Heat level follows how hard the user presses.

ideas.rationale: Pressing harder for more heat is an intuitive action that needs no training.

ideas.title: Dinner-Bell Melody

new_nodes.label: Melody announcer
new_nodes.detail: Plays a short tune that rises in tempo as the food nears completion.

new_nodes.label: Announce by melody
new_nodes.detail: Progress is announced through a tune.

ideas.rationale: A tune that speeds up needs no reading and is easy to notice from another room.

ideas.title: Weight-Sensing Auto-Cook Plate

new_nodes.label: Load-cell food plate
new_nodes.detail: Turntable sits on a load cell that reads food mass and starts the cycle automatically.

new_nodes.label: Load-cell lookup-table cooking
new_nodes.detail: Mass maps to a built-in time and power table, so no user settings are needed.

ideas.rationale: The user places food and presses start, so there is nothing to set, read, or learn.

ideas.title: Pictogram Dial Replacing Numbers

new_nodes.label: Food-picture dial
new_nodes.detail: One dial whose positions show pictures of soup, bread, leftovers and popcorn instead of numbers.

ideas.rationale: Users choose by recognising the food rather than interpreting minutes and power percentages.

ideas.title: NFC Food Tag Self-Programming

new_nodes.label: NFC food-tag reader
new_nodes.detail: A reader pad that reads a tag on the food packaging and sets time and power automatically.

new_nodes.label: Passive NFC tag encoding
new_nodes.detail: Ready meals carry a cheap printed NFC tag that stores their cooking profile.

ideas.rationale: Placing the packaged meal on the pad is the only action required, with no settings to understand.

ideas.title: Barcode Card Slot

new_nodes.label: Printed instruction card slot
new_nodes.detail: The user slides in a card printed with a barcode for the food, and the machine cooks to match.

ideas.rationale: Sliding in a card is a physical action that needs no reading or knob-turning.

ideas.title: Voice Command Without an App

new_nodes.label: Offline wake-word chip
new_nodes.detail: An onboard chip responds to a few spoken phrases such as 'warm soup' with no phone or app.

new_nodes.label: Embedded keyword spotting
new_nodes.detail: A low-cost on-device speech model recognises a small fixed vocabulary.

ideas.rationale: Speaking a natural phrase needs no manual, and it suits elderly users whose hands are unsteady.

ideas.title: Tap-the-Picture Touchscreen

new_nodes.label: Large-icon touch panel
new_nodes.detail: A panel with four large photos of common foods that starts the cycle on tap.

ideas.rationale: A single tap on a recognisable photo gives an immediate result with no menus to navigate.

ideas.title: Wave-to-Start Gesture

new_nodes.label: Infrared gesture sensor
new_nodes.detail: A sensor on the front detects a wave or hand motion and opens or starts the unit.

new_nodes.label: Passive infrared motion detection
new_nodes.detail: Low-power IR sensing is cheap and needs no contact.

ideas.rationale: A natural hand wave is intuitive and removes any need to find or press a button.

ideas.title: Proximity Door Opener

new_nodes.label: Capacitive proximity door latch
new_nodes.detail: The door unlatches when a hand approaches, with a spring pushing it slightly open.

ideas.rationale: The door responds to an approaching hand, so the user never has to find the release point.

ideas.title: Tilt-to-Open Door

new_nodes.label: Gravity-balanced door
new_nodes.detail: The door is counterweighted so a gentle push or pull opens it with no latch or button.

ideas.rationale: A door that opens with an intuitive push needs no mechanism to understand.

ideas.title: Top-Loading Drop-In Drawer

new_nodes.label: Top-loading lid
new_nodes.detail: A flip-up lid over the cavity removes the front door and its hinges entirely.

ideas.rationale: Lifting a lid and dropping food in mirrors how people already use a bowl or pot.

ideas.title: Transparent Conductive Door Window

new_nodes.label: Transparent conductive oxide film
new_nodes.detail: A thin oxide coating on glass reflects microwaves while letting light through.

ideas.rationale: A clear door lets users see the food, so they never need to open it to check.

ideas.title: Fully Glass Cavity Without Lamp

new_nodes.label: Glass cavity wall
new_nodes.detail: The cavity is lined with a tinted glass that stays lit by ambient light from the kitchen.

ideas.rationale: Ambient light keeps the food visible without a bulb to switch on or replace.

ideas.title: Ambient Colour Ring Status Light

new_nodes.label: Colour ring light
new_nodes.detail: A ring around the cavity glows green while cooking and turns to a steady colour when done.

ideas.rationale: Colour states mean something everywhere, so no numbers or reading are needed to know the status.

ideas.title: Progress Bar Replacing Countdown

new_nodes.label: Filling progress strip
new_nodes.detail: A horizontal strip on the door fills with colour as cooking progresses.

ideas.rationale: A visible fill shows progress without needing to read numbers or handle the timer's imprecision.

ideas.title: Steam-Sensed Auto-Stop

new_nodes.label: Humidity sensor
new_nodes.detail: A humidity sensor in the vent stops cooking when steam output drops off.

new_nodes.label: Vapour-based closed-loop control
new_nodes.detail: Steam output is used as a proxy for food doneness.

ideas.rationale: The machine decides when food is done, so the user needs no timing decisions at all.

ideas.title: Popcorn-Style Acoustic Stop

new_nodes.label: Acoustic sensor
new_nodes.detail: A microphone listens for the crackle of popping or boiling and ends the cycle at the right moment.

ideas.rationale: Listening for the food's own signal removes timing guesswork for anyone.

ideas.title: Thermocouple Probe Finish

new_nodes.label: Heat-sensing probe
new_nodes.detail: A probe is inserted into the food and stops cooking at a set temperature.

ideas.rationale: Stopping on temperature means the user never has to judge done-ness.

ideas.title: Sand-Glass Analog Timer

new_nodes.label: Fill-and-drain sand chamber
new_nodes.detail: A fixed sand chamber drains over the cooking time and ends the cycle when empty.

ideas.rationale: A visible draining sand shows time passing, which is easier to grasp than any digital display.

ideas.title: Haptic Done Mat

new_nodes.label: Vibrating base pad
new_nodes.detail: The base vibrates gently when cooking ends, so users know without hearing a bell.

ideas.rationale: A tactile alert is clear for elderly users who may be hard of hearing.

ideas.title: Scent Release Done Signal

new_nodes.label: Scent cartridge
new_nodes.detail: A scent pulses into the room when cooking finishes so the user knows it is done.

ideas.rationale: A smell is a signal that works without sight or sound, which suits users with limited senses.

ideas.title: Spoken Done Announcement

new_nodes.label: Speech synthesis chip
new_nodes.detail: The machine says 'Your food is ready' when cooking ends.

ideas.rationale: A plain spoken message needs no interpretation of sounds or lights.

ideas.title: Two-Button Hot and Done

new_nodes.label: Hot and Done buttons
new_nodes.detail: Two large buttons: Hot heats a standard portion, Done stops the cycle.

ideas.rationale: Two self-explanatory buttons remove every decision except whether to heat or stop.

ideas.title: Single Rotary Food-Colour Dial

new_nodes.label: Colour-ring rotary dial
new_nodes.detail: One dial with coloured zones: red for meat, green for vegetables, blue for drinks.

ideas.rationale: Matching colours to food types replaces two dials with one intuitive choice.

ideas.title: Fixed Power, Smart Pulse Rhythm

new_nodes.label: Adaptive pulse controller
new_nodes.detail: The firmware picks an on/off rhythm for each food type, so the user never sees a power setting.

ideas.rationale: Hiding power selection in firmware removes the need to choose any level.

ideas.title: Two-State Gentle or Full Switch

new_nodes.label: Gentle/Full slider
new_nodes.detail: A slider with only two positions, Gentle and Full, mapped to fixed duty cycles.

ideas.rationale: Two options are easier to understand than five, with no meaningless middle steps.

ideas.title: Smiley Face Power Control

new_nodes.label: Expression power dial
new_nodes.detail: The power dial shows a smile for gentle heating and a grin for strong heating.

ideas.rationale: Facial expressions carry meaning across languages and literacy levels.

ideas.title: Food-Type Slider Replacing Power

new_nodes.label: Frozen-to-leftover slider
new_nodes.detail: A slider running from frozen to leftover that sets power by food state.

ideas.rationale: Choosing by food state is more natural than choosing an abstract power percentage.

ideas.title: Tone-Pitch Power Feedback

new_nodes.label: Tone generator
new_nodes.detail: A rising pitch tells the user the power is high; a falling pitch means low.

ideas.rationale: Pitch gives instant feedback on heat level without any visual reading.

ideas.title: Automatic Mains Voltage Sensing

new_nodes.label: Universal auto-ranging power supply
new_nodes.detail: A single supply accepts 100–240 V at 50 or 60 Hz and adjusts itself.

ideas.rationale: One model works everywhere, so users never need to check a voltage label.

ideas.title: Retractable Sliding Door Panel

new_nodes.label: Sliding glass panel
new_nodes.detail: A door panel slides sideways on a rail instead of swinging on hinges.

ideas.rationale: A door that slides needs no clearance and no decision about which way to swing.

ideas.title: Magnetic Self-Closing Door

new_nodes.label: Magnetic catch
new_nodes.detail: A magnet pulls the door shut and holds it closed with no latch to press.

ideas.rationale: The door closes on its own, so the user never needs to check it or operate a latch.

ideas.title: Suction Cup Door Pull

new_nodes.label: Vacuum seal door pull
new_nodes.detail: A large suction handle on the door releases when pulled, with no separate button.

ideas.rationale: Pulling the handle to open is the most natural action, and it needs no button to find.

ideas.title: Glowing Hot-Zone Door Sticker

new_nodes.label: Photoluminescent press zone
new_nodes.detail: A glowing area on the door marks exactly where to press, without any button shape.

ideas.rationale: A glowing target shows the user where to press, even in dim kitchens.

ideas.title: Edge Capacitive Touch Strip

new_nodes.label: Capacitive door-edge strip
new_nodes.detail: A touch strip along the door edge opens the door when touched.

ideas.rationale: A long touch zone is hard to miss and needs no precise pressing.

ideas.title: Drop-Down Microwave Drawer

new_nodes.label: Pull-out cavity drawer
new_nodes.detail: The cavity slides out like a drawer, with food placed on a tray.

ideas.rationale: Drawers are familiar objects, so the user loads food the way they open a kitchen drawer.

ideas.title: Rotating Drum Door

new_nodes.label: Rotating drum cavity
new_nodes.detail: A drum rotates to bring the opening to the front, so no separate door is needed.

ideas.rationale: A rotating drum is a single movement, which avoids hinges, latches and interlocks.

ideas.title: Stationary Stirring Tray

new_nodes.label: Self-stirring tray
new_nodes.detail: A tray with a built-in paddle mixes food so the turntable is no longer needed.

ideas.rationale: Stirring happens automatically, so the user never has to rotate or reposition the food.

ideas.title: Moulded Recyclable Shell

new_nodes.label: Injection-moulded polymer housing
new_nodes.detail: The wrapper is a single moulded shell instead of a stamped steel one.

ideas.rationale: A cheap moulded housing lowers cost, which lets the savings go into simpler controls.

ideas.title: Snap-Fit Modular Assembly

new_nodes.label: Snap-fit tool-free assembly
new_nodes.detail: Panels snap together with no screws or welds.

ideas.rationale: Simpler assembly cuts cost, so the low-price tier can afford better, simpler controls.

ideas.title: Conductive Plastic Cavity

new_nodes.label: Metal-filled conductive polymer
new_nodes.detail: A plastic with embedded conductive fibres shields microwaves in place of steel sheet.

ideas.rationale: A moulded cavity cuts tooling and assembly steps, making the product cheaper to build.

ideas.title: Countertop Tile Microwave

new_nodes.label: Flat heating tile
new_nodes.detail: A thin flat panel sits on the counter, heating a plate placed on top.

ideas.rationale: A flat surface needs no door, so there is nothing to open, close or latch.

ideas.title: Under-Cabinet Built-In Heater

new_nodes.label: Under-cabinet heating shelf
new_nodes.detail: A shelf fitted under a kitchen cabinet heats food placed on it, with no visible controls.

ideas.rationale: Built into the kitchen, it is always there and needs no separate appliance to learn.

ideas.title: Fridge-Door Reheater

new_nodes.label: Fridge-integrated heating panel
new_nodes.detail: A heating panel built into the refrigerator door warms food placed on a shelf.

ideas.rationale: Reheating happens where food is already stored, so no extra step or appliance is needed.

ideas.title: Self-Heating Meal Pod

new_nodes.label: Sealed heating pod
new_nodes.detail: A pre-packed meal contains its own heating element, triggered by one press.

ideas.rationale: The meal carries its own heating, so the user does nothing but press once.

ideas.title: Microwave-Free Food Tray

new_nodes.label: Microwave-absorbing susceptor film
new_nodes.detail: A film in the food tray absorbs microwaves and heats food directly.

ideas.rationale: Packaging does the heating work, so the machine's controls can be fewer.

ideas.title: Child-Proof Auto-Lock Door

new_nodes.label: Auto-lock safety catch
new_nodes.detail: A safety catch that locks automatically when cooking starts, with no key or switch.

ideas.rationale: Safety is handled automatically, so no one needs to remember a lock sequence.

ideas.title: Fully Automatic Open-Close Cycle

new_nodes.label: Motorised door actuator
new_nodes.detail: A small motor opens the door at the end of cooking and closes it when the food is placed.

ideas.rationale: The door opens and closes by itself, so the user never has to work the mechanism.

ideas.title: Radiation Leakage Indicator Light

new_nodes.label: Leakage warning strip
new_nodes.detail: A strip on the door changes colour if the seal is compromised, so users know it is safe.

ideas.rationale: A simple colour check gives users confidence in safety without any technical knowledge.

ideas.title: Single Preset for Every Food

new_nodes.label: One-touch universal preset
new_nodes.detail: A single button runs a universal preset that adapts time and power to the food inside.

ideas.rationale: One button for every food removes all decisions and any need for a manual.

ideas.title: Tactile Braille-Style Dial

new_nodes.label: Raised-bump dial
new_nodes.detail: Dial positions are marked with raised bumps so they can be felt without looking.

ideas.rationale: Users can set the dial by touch alone, which suits people with poor eyesight.

ideas.title: Ready-Meal Scan Cooking

new_nodes.label: Camera food recogniser
new_nodes.detail: A camera identifies the food on the plate and sets the cycle automatically.

new_nodes.label: On-device image classification
new_nodes.detail: A small vision model classifies common foods without a network.

ideas.rationale: Pointing at food is all that is needed, so the user never has to choose a setting.

ideas.title: Plug-and-Play Smart Plate Ring

new_nodes.label: Power-sensing plate ring
new_nodes.detail: A ring placed under the bowl reads what it contains and sets power to match.

ideas.rationale: Placing the dish on the ring is the only action, and the power follows automatically.

ideas.title: Light-Pulse Done Indicator

new_nodes.label: Pulsing done light
new_nodes.detail: The cavity light pulses slowly when food is ready and stays still while cooking.

ideas.rationale: A pulsing light is an obvious signal that needs no reading of numbers or sounds.

ideas.title: Lid-Open Auto-Pause

new_nodes.label: Door-open auto-pause sensor
new_nodes.detail: Opening the door pauses cooking and resumes it when the door closes, with no restart needed.

ideas.rationale: Opening the door is intuitive and safe, so users never have to remember to restart.

ideas.title: One-Dial Context Cooking

new_nodes.label: Single context-aware dial
new_nodes.detail: One detented dial whose position is interpreted by a small MCU as a food category, replacing separate timer and power knobs.

ideas.rationale: A single dial with food-category presets removes the need to understand two independent numeric controls.

ideas.title: Weigh-and-Go Turntable

new_nodes.label: Load-cell turntable weighing
new_nodes.detail: Strain gauges under the turntable estimate food mass and set time automatically.

ideas.rationale: Users place food and press start, so no timer setting is needed.

ideas.title: Packet-Programmed Cooking

new_nodes.label: NFC tag on food packaging
new_nodes.detail: Tapping the packet on the fascia loads the manufacturer's cook program.

ideas.rationale: The packaging does the programming, so the user only taps and presses start.

ideas.title: Recipe Card Slot

new_nodes.label: Recipe card slot
new_nodes.detail: A slot on the fascia that accepts a printed card whose pattern sets time and power.

ideas.rationale: Inserting a card that looks like a kids' game card gives instant results with zero settings.

ideas.title: Spoken One-Word Cooking

new_nodes.label: Offline keyword recognition
new_nodes.detail: A tiny on-device speech model recognises a few words such as warm, defrost and ready.

ideas.rationale: Speaking a single word needs no reading, which suits elderly and visually impaired users.

ideas.title: Picture-Dial Power

new_nodes.label: Food-picture power dial
new_nodes.detail: Power dial printed with pictures of food (soup, bread, ice) instead of numbers.

ideas.rationale: Users choose by picture rather than by understanding duty cycles.

ideas.title: Door Ring Progress Light

new_nodes.label: Colour LED door ring
new_nodes.detail: A ring of LEDs around the door that fills as cooking progresses and turns green when done.

ideas.rationale: A progress ring shows status at a glance without the user needing to interpret anything.

ideas.title: Door Pops Open When Done

new_nodes.label: Spring-assisted door ajar
new_nodes.detail: A spring nudges the door a few millimetres ajar at the end of cooking.

ideas.rationale: The door itself signals completion, which needs no sound and no reading.

ideas.title: Scent Done Cue

new_nodes.label: Aroma cartridge
new_nodes.detail: A small cartridge releases a warm bread or cinnamon scent when cooking ends.

ideas.rationale: A smell cue tells the user food is ready without any setting or interpretation.

ideas.title: Wristband Done Buzz

new_nodes.label: Bluetooth wristband
new_nodes.detail: A wearable that vibrates when the appliance finishes, paired once by the family.

ideas.rationale: Vibration reaches users who are deaf or who walk away, with no setup beyond one pairing.

ideas.title: Touch-Anywhere Door

new_nodes.label: Push-to-open magnetic latch
new_nodes.detail: A magnetic latch that opens when the door is pressed anywhere along its edge.

ideas.rationale: Pressing the door opens it, so no one needs to search for a release button.

ideas.title: Foot-Kick Door Release

new_nodes.label: Floor kick plate
new_nodes.detail: A low plate at the base that opens the door when kicked, for users with full hands.

ideas.rationale: A kick plate works with full hands and needs no aim or learning.

ideas.title: Sliding Drawer Door

new_nodes.label: Sliding glass drawer front
new_nodes.detail: The door slides sideways on a rail, so nothing needs to swing open or clear space.

ideas.rationale: A drawer motion is intuitive and removes the hinge-swing problem entirely.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Doneness Window

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic window film
new_nodes.detail: A film that changes colour when the food reaches a serving temperature.

ideas.rationale: The window visually reveals doneness, so the user does not need to open the door to check.

ideas.title: Solid-State Cooking Engine

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Transistor amplifiers at 2.45 GHz replace the magnetron, transformer and HV chain.

ideas.rationale: Removing the lethal high-voltage chain removes the fear of electric shock for families.

ideas.title: Continuous Power Without Clicks

new_nodes.label: Continuous RF power modulation
new_nodes.detail: Solid-state drive gives smooth power output with no on/off ticking.

ideas.rationale: A power setting then works exactly as it is labelled, with nothing hidden in duty cycles.

ideas.title: Inductive Base Plate

new_nodes.label: Inductive power transfer base
new_nodes.detail: The oven sits on a base pad that transfers power wirelessly, with the same design for all mains voltages.

ideas.rationale: No plug to find or insert means the oven is always ready to use.

ideas.title: Mode Stirrer Instead of Turntable

new_nodes.label: Rotating mode stirrer
new_nodes.detail: A metal fan blade in the cavity roof spreads microwaves without moving the food.

ideas.rationale: With nothing to load or align, the user just places food on a flat floor.

ideas.title: Vibrating Stir Tray

new_nodes.label: Electromagnetic vibration drive
new_nodes.detail: A solenoid gently shakes the tray to move food, replacing a rotating motor.

ideas.rationale: A simple vibrating tray needs no belts or rollers that may need fitting.

ideas.title: Passive Heat-Pipe Cooling
